children.translated_text: <s>Devīgītā</s>

children.text:
atha prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha ekatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now the first chapter —
Seventh Book
Now the thirty-first chapter
<s>Janamejaya</s> said:
On the crown of the lord of the earth's support, that supreme radiance manifested,

children.text: yaduktaṃ bhavatā pūrvaṃ vistarāttadvadasva me // Dg_1.1 = DbhP_7,31.1 //
children.translated_text: which you previously described at length—tell me that in detail. // Dg_1.1 = DbhP_7,31.1 //
What wise person could become dispassionate while drinking the nectar of stories of <s>Śakti</s>?

children.text: sudhāṃ tu pibatāṃ mṛtyuḥ sa naitacchṛṇvato bhavet // Dg_1.2 = DbhP_7,31.2 //
children.translated_text: Death comes to those who drink <s>sudhā</s> (nectar of immortality), but not to those who listen to this. // Dg_1.2 = DbhP_7,31.2 //
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
You are blessed, you have accomplished your purpose, you have been instructed by great souls,

children.text: bhāgyavānasi yaddevyāṃ nirvyājā bhaktirasti te // Dg_1.3 = DbhP_7,31.3 //
children.translated_text: you are fortunate, for you have sincere devotion to the <s>Devī</s>. // Dg_1.3 = DbhP_7,31.3 //
Listen, O king, to what happened long ago when <s>Satī</s>'s body was consumed by fire:

children.text: bhrāntaḥ śivastu babhrāma kvaciddeśe sthiro 'bhavat // Dg_1.4 = DbhP_7,31.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, distraught, wandered about and came to rest in a certain place. // Dg_1.4 = DbhP_7,31.4 //
Free from awareness of the phenomenal world, his mind absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (deep meditation),

children.text: dhyāyandevīsvarūpaṃ tu kālaṃ ninye sa ātmavān // Dg_1.5 = DbhP_7,31.5 //
children.translated_text: meditating on the true form of the <s>Devī</s>, that self-possessed one passed the time. // Dg_1.5 = DbhP_7,31.5 //
The three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings became bereft of auspiciousness,

children.text: śaktihīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sābdhidvīpaṃ saparvatam // Dg_1.6 = DbhP_7,31.6 //
children.translated_text: the entire universe with its oceans, islands, and mountains became devoid of <s>Śakti</s> (divine power). // Dg_1.6 = DbhP_7,31.6 //
Joy dried up within the hearts of all,
all the worlds became indifferent, their minds shattered by anxiety. // Dg_1.7 = DbhP_7,31.7 //
Always sunk in an ocean of sorrow, they became afflicted by disease,

children.text: grahāṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca vaiparītyena vartanam // Dg_1.8 = DbhP_7,31.8 //
children.translated_text: and the planets and deities moved in contrary fashion. // Dg_1.8 = DbhP_7,31.8 //
Due to the absence of the lords of the material and divine spheres, O king, they were helpless.

children.text: atha 'sminneva kāle tu tārakākhyo mahasuraḥ // Dg_1.9 = DbhP_7,31.9 //
children.translated_text: Then at that very time, the great <s>asura</s> named <s>Tāraka</s> // Dg_1.9 = DbhP_7,31.9 //
that <s>daitya</s> (demon), endowed with a boon from <s>Brahmā</s>, became the ruler of the three worlds.

children.text: śivaurasastu yaḥ putraḥ sa te hantā bhaviṣyati // Dg_1.10 = DbhP_7,31.10 //
children.translated_text: "He who is the son born of <s>Śiva</s>'s seed shall be your slayer" — // Dg_1.10 = DbhP_7,31.10 //
thus was the death of that great <s>asura</s> ordained by the gods of gods,

children.text: śivairasasutābhāvājjagarja ca nananda ca // Dg_1.11 = DbhP_7,31.11 //
children.translated_text: and since there was no son born of <s>Śiva</s>'s seed, he roared and rejoiced. // Dg_1.11 = DbhP_7,31.11 //
Harassed by him, all the gods were driven from their abodes,
and because there was no son born of <s>Śiva</s>'s seed, they fell into insurmountable anxiety. // Dg_1.12 = DbhP_7,31.12 //
"<s>Śaṅkara</s> has no consort—how then can his son come into being?

children.text: asmākaṃ bhāgyahīnānāṃ kathaṃ kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati // Dg_1.13 = DbhP_7,31.13 //
children.translated_text: How will the purpose of us unfortunate ones be accomplished?" // Dg_1.13 = DbhP_7,31.13 //
Thus anxious, they all went to the realm of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: śaśaṃsurharimekānte sa copāyaṃ jagāda ha // Dg_1.14 = DbhP_7,31.14 //
children.translated_text: and told <s>Hari</s> in private, and he spoke a remedy: // Dg_1.14 = DbhP_7,31.14 //
"Why are you all anxious? The auspicious <s>Śivā</s>, the wish-fulfilling tree of desires,
the sovereign of the worlds, dweller in <s>Maṇidvīpa</s> (the Jewel Island), is awake! // Dg_1.15 = DbhP_7,31.15 //
It is only because of our own misdeeds that she is indifferent, not otherwise.
This is but a lesson given to us by the Mother of the World, for our discipline. // Dg_1.16 = DbhP_7,31.16 //
Just as a mother, whether caressing or striking, has no lack of compassion toward her child,
even so does the Mother of the World regulate merits and faults. // Dg_1.17 = DbhP_7,31.17 //
A son commits offenses at every step—

children.text: ko 'paraḥ sahate loke kevalaṃ mātaraṃ vinā // Dg_1.18 = DbhP_7,31.18 //
children.translated_text: who else in the world can bear them except the mother alone? // Dg_1.18 = DbhP_7,31.18 //

children.text: tasmadyūyaṃ parāmbāṃ tāṃ śaraṇaṃ yāta mā ciram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, go without delay to that Supreme Mother as your refuge,

children.text: nirvyājayā cittavṛttyā sā vaḥ kāryaṃ vidhāsyati // Dg_1.19 = DbhP_7,31.19 //
children.translated_text: with a sincere mental disposition—she will accomplish your purpose." // Dg_1.19 = DbhP_7,31.19 //
Having thus instructed all the gods, the great <s>Viṣṇu</s>, accompanied by his consort,

children.text: saṃyuto nirjagāmāśu devaiḥ saha surādhipaḥ // Dg_1.20 = DbhP_7,31.20 //
children.translated_text: went forth swiftly, the lord of the gods, together with the gods. // Dg_1.20 = DbhP_7,31.20 //
He came to the great mountain, <s>Himavān</s>, the king of mountains,

children.text: abhavaṃśca surāḥ sarve puraścaraṇakarmiṇaḥ // Dg_1.21 = DbhP_7,31.21 //
children.translated_text: and all the gods performed preparatory rites (<s>puraścaraṇa</s>). // Dg_1.21 = DbhP_7,31.21 //
Knowledgeable in the ritual of the sacrifice to the Mother, they performed the <s>Ambā-yajña</s> (sacrifice to the Mother),

children.text: tṛtīyādivratānyāśu cakruḥ sarve surā nṛpa // Dg_1.22 = DbhP_7,31.22 //
children.translated_text: and all the gods, O king, quickly performed vows such as the third-day fast. // Dg_1.22 = DbhP_7,31.22 //
Some were absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>, some were devoted to reciting her name,
some were devoted to hymns (<s>sūkta</s>), some were eager in the complete recitation of her names. // Dg_1.23 = DbhP_7,31.23 //
Some were devoted to the complete recitation of <s>mantras</s>, some were performing austerities like <s>kṛcchra</s>,
some were devoted to the inner sacrifice (<s>antaryāga</s>), some were devoted to <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement). // Dg_1.24 = DbhP_7,31.24 //
They worshipped the Supreme <s>Śakti</s> with the <s>Hrīṃ</s>-syllable, unwearied.
Thus many years passed, O <s>Janamejaya</s>. // Dg_1.25 = DbhP_7,31.25 //
Suddenly, on the ninth day of the month of <s>Caitra</s>, on a Friday,
there appeared before them that radiance spoken of in the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas). // Dg_1.26 = DbhP_7,31.26 //
Praised in the four directions by the four <s>Vedas</s> in embodied form,
resplendent as ten million suns, cool as ten million moons, // Dg_1.27 = DbhP_7,31.27 //
equal in radiance to ten million lightning bolts, that reddish supreme radiance

children.text: naiva cordhvaṃ na tiryakca na madhye parijagrabhat // Dg_1.28 = DbhP_7,31.28 //
children.translated_text: was grasped neither above, nor sideways, nor in the middle. // Dg_1.28 = DbhP_7,31.28 //
It was without beginning or end, not possessing hands or other limbs,

children.text: na ca strīrūpamathavā na puṃrūpamathobhayam // Dg_1.29 = DbhP_7,31.29 //
children.translated_text: neither in the form of a woman, nor in the form of a man, nor both. // Dg_1.29 = DbhP_7,31.29 //
Its brilliance caused the covering of the eyes of those gods, O king.

children.text: punaśca dhairyamālambya yāvatte dadṛśuḥ surāḥ // Dg_1.30 = DbhP_7,31.30 //
children.translated_text: Then again, gathering their courage, as they looked, // Dg_1.30 = DbhP_7,31.30 //
that very same radiance shone forth in the divine, enchanting form of a woman,

children.text: atīva ramaṇīyāṅgīṃ kumārīṃ navayauvanām // Dg_1.31 = DbhP_7,31.31 //
children.translated_text: an exceedingly beautiful-limbed maiden in the bloom of youth, // Dg_1.31 = DbhP_7,31.31 //
whose pair of upraised, full breasts put to shame the lotus bud,
with tinkling nets of small bells, jingling anklets, and a girdle, // Dg_1.32 = DbhP_7,31.32 //
adorned with golden armlets, bracelets, and a necklace,
resplendent with a throat-ornament set with priceless gems, // Dg_1.33 = DbhP_7,31.33 //
with dark tresses where bees hovered like slender <s>ketaka</s> (pandanus) flowers,
graced by the beauty of her hips and adorned with a line of fine hair, // Dg_1.34 = DbhP_7,31.34 //
her face filled with <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) mixed with pieces of camphor,
her lotus-face graced by shining golden ear-ornaments, // Dg_1.35 = DbhP_7,31.35 //
her forehead like the crescent moon on the eighth day, with long eyebrows,
with eyes like red lotuses, a prominent nose, and sweet lips, // Dg_1.36 = DbhP_7,31.36 //
with teeth whose tips were like <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds, resplendent with a pearl necklace,
wearing a crown set with gems, bearing a crescent moon. // Dg_1.37 = DbhP_7,31.37 //
Her tresses of hair resplendent with garlands of <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) and <s>mālatī</s> (night-jasmine),
a dot of saffron on her forehead, sporting three eyes, // Dg_1.38 = DbhP_7,31.38 //
four-armed, bearing a noose (<s>pāśa</s>), a goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), a boon-granting gesture (<s>vara</s>), and a fear-dispelling gesture (<s>abhīti</s>), three-eyed,
wearing red garments, with the radiance of a pomegranate blossom, // Dg_1.39 = DbhP_7,31.39 //
endowed with all ornamental beauty, worshipped by all gods,
the fulfiller of all hopes, the mother of all, the enchantress of all, // Dg_1.40 = DbhP_7,31.40 //
gracious-faced, the Mother, with a gentle smile on her lotus-face,

children.text: avyājakaruṇāmūrtiṃ dadṛśuḥ purataḥ surāḥ // Dg_1.41 = DbhP_7,31.41 //
children.translated_text: the very embodiment of spontaneous compassion—the gods beheld her before them. // Dg_1.41 = DbhP_7,31.41 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāṃ karuṇāmurtiṃ praṇemuḥ sakalāḥ surāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen that embodiment of compassion, all the gods bowed down,
unable to speak a word, their voices choked with tears. // Dg_1.42 = DbhP_7,31.42 //
Somehow regaining their composure, with devotion and bowed necks,
their eyes filled with tears of love, they praised the Mother of the World: // Dg_1.43 = DbhP_7,31.43 //
The gods said:

children.text: namo devyai mahādevyai śivāyai satataṃ namaḥ /
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Devī</s>, to the great <s>Devī</s>, to the auspicious one (<s>Śivā</s>), perpetual homage!

children.text: namaḥ prakṛtyai bhadrāyai niyatāḥ praṇatāḥ sma tām // Dg_1.44 = DbhP_7,31.44 //
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), to the beneficent one! We bow down before her, devoted. // Dg_1.44 = DbhP_7,31.44 //

children.text: tām agnivarṇāṃ tapasā jvalantīṃ vairocanīṃ karmaphaleṣu juṣṭām /
children.translated_text: To her who is fire-colored, blazing with <s>tapas</s> (austerity), who is the radiant one, resorted to for the fruits of action,

children.text: durgāṃ devīṃ śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye sutarasi tarase namaḥ // Dg_1.45 = DbhP_7,31.45 //
children.translated_text: <s>Durgā</s>, the <s>Devī</s>—I take refuge! Homage to her who carries across, to the deliverer! // Dg_1.45 = DbhP_7,31.45 //

children.text: devīṃ vācamajanayanta devāstāṃ viśvarūpāḥ paśavo vadanti /
children.translated_text: The gods gave birth to the <s>Devī</s> of Speech; the creatures of all forms speak her.

children.text: sā no mandreṣamūrjaṃ duhānā dhenur vāgasmānupasuṣṭutaitu // Dg_1.46 = DbhP_7,31.46 //
children.translated_text: May she, the cow of speech, yielding strength and nourishment with her lowing, come well-praised to us! // Dg_1.46 = DbhP_7,31.46 //
To <s>Kālarātrī</s> (the Night of Dissolution), praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, the Mother of <s>Skanda</s>,

children.text: sarasvatīmaditiṃ dakṣaduhitaraṃ namāmaḥ pāvanāṃ śivām // Dg_1.47 = DbhP_7,31.47 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, to <s>Aditi</s>, to the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>—we bow to the purifying <s>Śivā</s>. // Dg_1.47 = DbhP_7,31.47 //

children.text: mahālakṣmyai ca vidmahe sarvaśaktyai ca dhīmahi /
children.translated_text: We meditate upon <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, we contemplate the all-<s>Śakti</s>,
may that <s>Devī</s> inspire us! // Dg_1.48 = DbhP_7,31.48 //
Homage to her whose form is the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic body)! Homage to her whose form is the <s>Sūtrātman</s> (the Thread-Self)!

children.text: namo 'vyākṛtarūpiṇyai namaḥ śrībrahma mūrtaye // Dg_1.49 = DbhP_7,31.49 //
children.translated_text: Homage to her whose form is the Unmanifest! Homage to her whose form is <s>Brahman</s>! // Dg_1.49 = DbhP_7,31.49 //
Through ignorance of whom the world appears, like a rope-snake, a garland, and so on,
through knowledge of whom it is dissolved—we bow to that Sovereign of the World! // Dg_1.50 = DbhP_7,31.50 //
We bow to her who is the referent of the word 'That' (<s>tat-pada-lakṣyārtha</s>), whose form is the one essence of consciousness,
whose form is undivided bliss, who is the ground of the import of the <s>Vedas</s>. // Dg_1.51 = DbhP_7,31.51 //
To her who transcends the five sheaths (<s>pañcakośa</s>), who is the witness of the three states (<s>avasthātraya</s>),
and again, to her who is the referent of the word 'You' (<s>tvam-pada-lakṣyārtha</s>), whose form is the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), // Dg_1.52 = DbhP_7,31.52 //
homage to her whose form is <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ)! Homage to her whose form is the <s>Hrīṃkāra</s>!

children.text: nānāmantrātmikāyai te karuṇāyai namo namaḥ // Dg_1.53 = DbhP_7,31.53 //
children.translated_text: To her whose essence is the manifold <s>mantras</s>, to that compassionate one, homage, homage! // Dg_1.53 = DbhP_7,31.53 //
Thus praised by the gods, the dweller of <s>Maṇidvīpa</s>

children.text: prāha vācā madhurayā mattakokilaniḥsvanā // Dg_1.54 = DbhP_7,31.54 //
children.translated_text: spoke with a sweet voice, like the cry of an intoxicated cuckoo: // Dg_1.54 = DbhP_7,31.54 //
The blessed <s>Dev��</s> said:
"Let the gods state their purpose, for which they have assembled here.

children.text: varadāhaṃ sadā bhaktakāmakalpadrumāsmi ca // Dg_1.55 = DbhP_7,31.55 //
children.translated_text: I am always the wish-fulfilling tree of desires for devotees, and I grant boons. // Dg_1.55 = DbhP_7,31.55 //

children.text: tiṣṭhantyāṃ mayi kā cintā yuṣmākaṃ bhaktiśālinām /
children.translated_text: While I exist, what anxiety can there be for you who are endowed with devotion?
I lift up my devotees from the ocean of sorrowful <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dg_1.56 = DbhP_7,31.56 //

children.text: iti pratijñāṃ me satyāṃ jānītha vibudhottamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Know this true promise of mine, O best of gods!"

children.text: iti premākulāṃ vāṇīṃ śrutvā santuṣṭamānasāḥ // Dg_1.57 = DbhP_7,31.57 //
children.translated_text: Having heard that speech filled with love, their minds satisfied, // Dg_1.57 = DbhP_7,31.57 //
the fearless immortals, O king, spoke of their own suffering.
The gods said:

children.text: nājñātaṃ kiñcidapyatra bhvatyāsti jagastraye // Dg_1.58 = DbhP_7,31.58 //
children.translated_text: "Nothing whatsoever is unknown to you, O <s>Parameśvarī</s> (Supreme Goddess), in the three worlds! // Dg_1.58 = DbhP_7,31.58 //
O omniscient one, whose very form is the witness of all, O Supreme Sovereign!

children.text: tārakeṇāsurendreṇa pīḍitāḥ smo divāniśam // Dg_1.59 = DbhP_7,31.59 //
children.translated_text: We are tormented day and night by <s>Tāraka</s>, the lord of the <s>asuras</s>. // Dg_1.59 = DbhP_7,31.59 //
His death has been ordained by <s>Brahmā</s> at the hands of a son born of <s>Śiva</s>'s body, O Auspicious One,

children.text: śivāṅganā tu naivāsti jānāsi tvaṃ maheśvari // Dg_1.60 = DbhP_7,31.60 //
children.translated_text: but <s>Śiva</s> has no consort—you know this, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>! // Dg_1.60 = DbhP_7,31.60 //
What indeed is to be said by lowly beings before the Omniscient One?
We have spoken this in outline—infer the rest, O Mother! // Dg_1.61 = DbhP_7,31.61 //
May there be unwavering devotion at your lotus feet always—
that is our chief prayer; the rest is for the sake of our bodily existence." // Dg_1.62 = DbhP_7,31.62 //

children.text: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā provāca parameśvarī /
children.translated_text: Having heard their words, the Supreme Goddess said:

children.text: mama śaktistu yā gaurī bhaviṣyati himālaye // Dg_1.63 = DbhP_7,31.63 //
children.translated_text: "My <s>Śakti</s>, who is <s>Gaurī</s>, shall come into being on <s>Himālaya</s>. // Dg_1.63 = DbhP_7,31.63 //

children.text: śivāya sā pradeyā syāt sā vaḥ kāryaṃ vidhāsyati /
children.translated_text: She shall be given to <s>Śiva</s>—she will accomplish your purpose.
May there be devotion at her lotus feet among you all, with reverence. // Dg_1.64 = DbhP_7,31.64 //
<s>Himālaya</s> indeed worships me in his mind with supreme devotion;

children.text: tatastasya gṛhe janma mama priyakaraṃ matam // Dg_1.65 = DbhP_7,31.65 //
children.translated_text: therefore, birth in his house is pleasing to me." // Dg_1.65 = DbhP_7,31.65 //
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
<s>Himālaya</s> too, hearing that exceedingly gracious speech,

children.text: bāṣpaiḥ saṃruddhakaṇṭhākṣo mahārājñīṃ vaco 'bravīt // Dg_1.66 = DbhP_7,31.66 //
children.translated_text: his throat and eyes choked with tears, spoke to the Great Queen: // Dg_1.66 = DbhP_7,31.66 //
"You make great the one whose grace you desire.

children.text: nocetkvāhaṃ jaḍaḥ sthāṇuḥ kva tvaṃ saccitsvarūpiṇī // Dg_1.67 = DbhP_7,31.67 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, what am I—inert, a mere post—and what are you, whose form is Being-Consciousness! // Dg_1.67 = DbhP_7,31.67 //
Inconceivable even through a hundred births is the fatherhood of you, O Sinless One,

children.text: aśvamedhādi puṇyairvā puṇyairvā tatsamādhijaiḥ // Dg_1.68 = DbhP_7,31.68 //
children.translated_text: even through the merits of <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) and other rites, or through the merits born of <s>samādhi</s>. // Dg_1.68 = DbhP_7,31.68 //
Today in the world there will be fame: 'The Mother of the World has become a daughter—

children.text: aho himālayasyāsya dhanyo 'sau bhāgyavāniti // Dg_1.69 = DbhP_7,31.69 //
children.translated_text: how blessed is this <s>Himālaya</s>, how fortunate!' // Dg_1.69 = DbhP_7,31.69 //

children.text: yasyāstu jaṭhare santi brahmāṇḍānāṃ ca koṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: She in whose belly are crores of cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>),

children.text: saiva yasya sutā jātā ko vā syāttatsamo bhuvi // Dg_1.70 = DbhP_7,31.70 //
children.translated_text: she herself is born as whose daughter—who on earth could be his equal? // Dg_1.70 = DbhP_7,31.70 //

children.text: na jāne 'smatpitṝṇāṃ kiṃ sthānaṃ syānnirmitaṃ param /
children.translated_text: I do not know what supreme abode has been created for our forefathers

children.text: etādṛśānāṃ vāsāya yeṣāṃ vaṃśe 'sti mādṛśaḥ // Dg_1.71 = DbhP_7,31.71 //
children.translated_text: for the residence of such ones, in whose lineage there is one like me. // Dg_1.71 = DbhP_7,31.71 //

children.text: idaṃ yathā ca dattaṃ me kṛpayā premapūrṇayā /
children.translated_text: Just as you have given this to me out of compassion full of love,

children.text: sarvavedāntasiddhaṃ ca tvadrūpaṃ brūhi me tathā // Dg_1.72 = DbhP_7,31.72 //
children.translated_text: so tell me also your true nature, established by all <s>Vedānta</s>. // Dg_1.72 = DbhP_7,31.72 //

children.text: yogaṃ ca bhaktisahitaṃ jñānaṃ ca śrutisammatam /
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> together with <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) approved by the <s>Śrutis</s>—

children.text: vadasva parameśāni tvamevāhaṃ yato bhaveḥ // Dg_1.73 = DbhP_7,31.73 //
children.translated_text: speak, O Supreme Goddess, for I am to become you!" // Dg_1.73 = DbhP_7,31.73 //
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Upon his words, with a pleased lotus-face,

children.text: vaktumārabhatāmbā sā rahasyaṃ śrutigūhitam // Dg_1.74 = DbhP_7,31.74 //
children.translated_text: the Mother began to speak the secret hidden in the <s>Śrutis</s>. // Dg_1.74 = DbhP_7,31.74 //

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāmekatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the first chapter in the <s>Devīgītā</s> —
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter of the seventh book of the <s>Devīgītā</s> in the great <s>Purāṇa</s>, the glorious <s>Devī Bhāgavata</s>.

children.text:
atha dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now the second chapter —
Seventh Book
Now the thirty-second chapter
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇvantu nirjarāḥ sarve vyāharantyā vaco mama /
children.translated_text: Let all the immortals listen to the words I speak,

children.text: yasya śravaṇamātreṇa madrūpatvaṃ prapadyate // Dg_2.1 = DbhP_7,32.1 //
children.translated_text: by merely hearing which one attains identity with my form. (Dg 2.1)
I alone existed before, and nothing else whatsoever, O lord of mountains;
that essential form was pure consciousness (<s>citsaṃvit</s>), known by the single name <s>Parabrahman</s> (supreme Brahman). (Dg 2.2)
Inconceivable, indescribable, beyond comparison, free from affliction—

children.text: tasya kācitsvataḥ siddhā śaktirmāyeti viśrutā // Dg_2.3 = DbhP_7,32.3 //
children.translated_text: of that [Brahman] there is a certain self-established power, renowned as <s>Māyā</s>. (Dg 2.3)

children.text: na satī sā nāsatī sā nobhayātmā virodhataḥ /
children.translated_text: She is neither existent nor non-existent, nor of both natures, due to contradiction;
she is something distinct from these, a real entity that exists always. (Dg 2.4)
She is like the heat of fire, like the radiance of the sun,

children.text: candrasya candrikeveyaṃ mameyaṃ sahajā dhruvā // Dg_2.5 = DbhP_7,32.5 //
children.translated_text: like the moonlight of the moon—she is my innate, eternal [power]. (Dg 2.5)

children.text: tasyāṃ karmaṇi jīvānāṃ jīvāḥ kālāśca sañcare /
children.translated_text: In her, the <s>karmas</s> of living beings, the living beings themselves, and time in their activity

children.text: abhedena vilīnāḥ syuḥ suṣuptau vyavahāravat // Dg_2.6 = DbhP_7,32.6 //
children.translated_text: are dissolved without distinction, as in deep sleep, according to conventional usage. (Dg 2.6)
Through conjunction with my own power, I assumed the nature of a seed;

children.text: svādhārāvaraṇāttasyā doṣatvaṃ ca samāgatam // Dg_2.7 = DbhP_7,32.7 //
children.translated_text: through that [power's] veiling of its own support, the quality of defect arose. (Dg 2.7)
Through conjunction with consciousness, she is called the instrumental cause;
through transformation into the manifest world, she is said to be the inherent cause. (Dg 2.8)
Some call her <s>tapas</s> (austerity), some <s>tamas</s> (darkness), others inert matter;

children.text: jñānaṃ māyāṃ pradhānaṃ ca prakṛtiṃ śaktimapyajām // Dg_2.9 = DbhP_7,32.9 //
children.translated_text: knowledge, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), power, and the unborn. (Dg 2.9)
Those skilled in <s>Śaiva</s> scriptures call her <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness);
others who contemplate the true meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> call her <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). (Dg 2.10)
Thus various names exist in the <s>Nigamas</s> (scriptures) and elsewhere.
Her inertness is due to being an object of perception; from the destruction of knowledge, she is [called] non-existent. (Dg 2.11)

children.text: caitanyasya na dṛśyatvam dṛśyatve jaḍameva tat /
children.translated_text: Consciousness is not an object of perception; if it were perceptible, it would be mere inert matter.

children.text: svaprakāśaṃ ca caitanyaṃ na pareṇa prakāśitam // Dg_2.12 = DbhP_7,32.12 //
children.translated_text: Consciousness is self-luminous and is not illuminated by another. (Dg 2.12)
Nor is it illuminated by itself, due to the fault of infinite regress;
there would be a contradiction between agent and action—therefore it is self-[luminous] like a lamp. (Dg 2.13)
Know, O Mountain, that while shining, it illuminates other things;

children.text: ata eva ca nityatvaṃ siddhasaṃvittanormama // Dg_2.14 = DbhP_7,32.14 //
children.translated_text: therefore the eternality of my nature as established consciousness is proven. (Dg 2.14)
In waking, dream, deep sleep, and other states, the objects of perception vary,

children.text: saṃvido vyabhicāraśca nānubhūto 'sti karhicit // Dg_2.15 = DbhP_7,32.15 //
children.translated_text: but the variation of consciousness itself has never been experienced. (Dg 2.15)
If its [consciousness's] absence too were experienced, then by what witness

children.text: anubhūtaḥ sa evātra śiṣṭaḥ saṃvidvapuḥ purā // Dg_2.16 = DbhP_7,32.16 //
children.translated_text: would it have been experienced? That very [witness] alone remains here—the body of consciousness from before. (Dg 2.16)

children.text: ata eva ca nityatvaṃ proktaṃ sacchāstrakovidaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore its eternality is declared by those skilled in the true scriptures.
And her nature is bliss, because she is the object of the supreme love of self. (Dg 2.17)

children.text: mā na bhūvaṃ hi bhūyāsamiti premātmani sthitam /
children.translated_text: "May I not cease to be; may I continue to exist"—such love is established in the self.

children.text: sarvasyānyasya mithyātvādasaṅgatvaṃ sphuṭaṃ mama // Dg_2.18 = DbhP_7,32.18 //
children.translated_text: Since everything else is false, my non-attachment is evident. (Dg 2.18)
Thus too my unlimitedness is held.

children.text: tacca jñānaṃ nātmadharmā dharmatve jaḍatātmanaḥ // Dg_2.19 = DbhP_7,32.19 //
children.translated_text: And that knowledge is not a property of the self; if it were a property, the self would be inert. (Dg 2.19)

children.text: jñānasya jaḍaśeṣatvaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ na ca saṃbhavi /
children.translated_text: That knowledge becomes a mere remnant of the inert has never been seen, nor is it possible;

children.text: ciddharmatvaṃ tathā nāsti citaścinna hi bhidyate // Dg_2.20 = DbhP_7,32.20 //
children.translated_text: likewise, consciousness-as-property does not exist, for consciousness is not divided. (Dg 2.20)
Therefore the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is always of the nature of knowledge and of the nature of bliss,

children.text: satyaḥ pūrṇo 'py asaṅgaśca dvaitajālavivarjitaḥ // Dg_2.21 = DbhP_7,32.21 //
children.translated_text: true, complete, unattached, and free from the web of duality. (Dg 2.21)
That [Self] again, through its own <s>Māyā</s> endowed with desire, <s>karma</s>, and the rest,
due to impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) from previous experience, and the ripening of time and <s>karma</s>, (Dg 2.22)
and due to non-discrimination of the truth, becomes possessed of the will to create.

children.text: abuddhipūrvaḥ sargo 'yaṃ kathitaste nagādhipa // Dg_2.23 = DbhP_7,32.23 //
children.translated_text: This creation is without deliberation—thus I have told you, O lord of mountains. (Dg 2.23)
That which I have spoken of as my supramundane form—
that is called the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the undifferentiated (<s>avyākṛta</s>), and also <s>Māyā</s>-variegated. (Dg 2.24)
It is declared in all scriptures as the cause of all causes,
the primordial among the principles (<s>tattvas</s>), of the form of <s>Saccidānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss). (Dg 2.25)
Condensed of all actions, the basis of will, knowledge, and activity,
expressible by the <s>Hrīṃkāra</s> mantra—that is called the primal principle (<s>āditattva</s>). (Dg 2.26)
From that arose space (<s>ākāśa</s>), of the nature of the sound <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element);
wind (<s>vāyu</s>) is of the nature of the touch [<s>tanmātra</s>], and fire (<s>tejas</s>) of the nature of form. (Dg 2.27)
Water (<s>jala</s>) is of the nature of taste, and then earth (<s>dharā</s>) is of the nature of smell.

children.text: śabdaikaguṇa ākāśo vāyuḥ sparśaravānvitaḥ // Dg_2.28 = DbhP_7,32.28 //
children.translated_text: Space has the single quality of sound; wind possesses touch and sound. (Dg 2.28)
Fire is declared by the wise to have the qualities of sound, touch, and form;
water is considered to have four qualities: sound, touch, form, and taste. (Dg 2.29)
Earth has five qualities: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell.
From those arose the great thread (<s>mahatsūtra</s>), which is designated the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>). (Dg 2.30)
That is declared to be the totality; it is the subtle body of the Self.

children.text: avyaktaṃ kāraṇo dehaḥ sa coktaḥ pūrvam eva hi // Dg_2.31 = DbhP_7,32.31 //
children.translated_text: The unmanifest is the causal body, which has already been described. (Dg 2.31)
In which the seed-form of the universe abides, from which the subtle body arises—

children.text: tataḥ sthūlāni bhūtāni pañcīkaraṇamārgataḥ // Dg_2.32 = DbhP_7,32.32 //
children.translated_text: from that, through the process of fivefold combination (<s>pañcīkaraṇa</s>), the gross elements, (Dg 2.32)
five in number, arise. That process is now described:

children.text: pūrvoktāni ca bhūtāni pratyekaṃ vibhajed dvidhā // Dg_2.33 = DbhP_7,32.33 //
children.translated_text: the previously mentioned elements are each divided into two halves. (Dg 2.33)
One half of each is divided into four parts, O Mountain.

children.text: svasvetaradvitīyāṃśe yojanātpañca pañca te // Dg_2.34 = DbhP_7,32.34 //
children.translated_text: By combining one's own half with one-fourth of each of the other four, the five [gross elements] arise. (Dg 2.34)
The product of that is the cosmic body (<s>Virāṭ</s>); this is the gross body of the Self.
From the <s>sattva</s> portions of the five elements, the organs of hearing and the rest arise. (Dg 2.35)
O king of kings, [these are] the organs of knowledge (<s>jñānendriyas</s>); from the combined [<s>sattva</s> portions],
the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is one, but fourfold in its functions. (Dg 2.36)

children.text: yadā tu saṅkalpavikalpakṛtyaṃ tadā bhavettanmana ityabhikhyam /
children.translated_text: When it performs the function of imagining and deliberating, it is called <s>manas</s> (mind);

children.text: syād buddhisaṃjñaṃ ca yadā pravetti suniścitaṃ saṃśayahīnarūpam // Dg_2.37 = DbhP_7,32.37 //
children.translated_text: when it proceeds to firm determination, free from doubt, it is named <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). (Dg 2.37)
In its function of continuous recollection, it is called <s>citta</s> (thought);

children.text: ahaṅkṛtyātmavṛttyā tu tadahaṅkāratāṃ gatam // Dg_2.38 = DbhP_7,32.38 //
children.translated_text: through the function of self-identification, it becomes <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego). (Dg 2.38)
From the <s>rajas</s> portions of those [elements], the organs of action (<s>karmendriyas</s>) arise in order;

children.text: pratyekaṃ militairtairtu prāṇo bhavati pañcadhā // Dg_2.39 = DbhP_7,32.39 //
children.translated_text: from the combined [<s>rajas</s> portions], <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) becomes fivefold. (Dg 2.39)
<s>Prāṇa</s> is in the heart; <s>apāna</s> is at the anus; <s>samāna</s> is at the navel;
<s>udāna</s> is in the throat region; <s>vyāna</s> pervades the entire body. (Dg 2.40)
The five organs of knowledge and the five organs of action,

children.text: prāṇādipañcakaṃ caiva dhiyāca sahitaṃ manaḥ // Dg_2.41 = DbhP_7,32.41 //
children.translated_text: the fivefold group of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, together with the intellect and <s>manas</s>— (Dg 2.41)
this is the subtle body, which is called my <s>liṅga</s> (mark).

children.text: tatra yā prakṛtiḥ proktā sā rājandvididhā smṛtā // Dg_2.42 = DbhP_7,32.42 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) previously described is, O king, held to be twofold: (Dg 2.42)
<s>Māyā</s> is of the nature of <s>sattva</s>; <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is mixed with the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: svāśrayaṃ yā tu saṃrakṣetsā māyeti nigadyate // Dg_2.43 = DbhP_7,32.43 //
children.translated_text: That which protects its own substrate is called <s>Māyā</s>. (Dg 2.43)
The reflection in her of the one who is the original, the Lord—

children.text: sa īśvaraḥ samākhyātaḥ svāśrayajñānavānparaḥ // Dg_2.44 = DbhP_7,32.44 //
children.translated_text: he is called <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the supreme one who possesses knowledge of his own substrate. (Dg 2.44)
He is omniscient, the maker of all, the bestower of all grace.

children.text: avidyāyāṃ tu yatkiñcitpratibimbaṃ nagādhipa // Dg_2.45 = DbhP_7,32.45 //
children.translated_text: But whatever reflection [appears] in <s>avidyā</s>, O lord of mountains— (Dg 2.45)
that is designated as the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), the basis of all suffering.
For both [Īśvara and jīva], the three bodies are declared through <s>avidyā</s>. (Dg 2.46)
Through identification with the three bodies, three names again arose.

children.text: prājñastu kāraṇātmā syātsūkṣmadehī tu taijasaḥ // Dg_2.47 = DbhP_7,32.47 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is the causal self; the one with the subtle body is <s>taijasa</s>. (Dg 2.47)
The one with the gross body is called <s>viśva</s>—thus the threefold [self] is declared.
Likewise, <s>Īśvara</s> too is described by the terms <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Sūtra</s>, and <s>Virāṭ</s>. (Dg 2.48)
The first is of the individual form; the latter is held to be of the collective form.

children.text: sa hi sarveśvaraḥ sākṣājjīvānugrahakāmyayā // Dg_2.49 = DbhP_7,32.49 //
children.translated_text: He indeed is the Lord of all; out of desire to grace the <s>jīvas</s>, (Dg 2.49)
he creates the manifold universe as the basis for various enjoyments,

children.text: macchaktiprerito nityaṃ mayi rājanprakalpitaḥ // Dg_2.50 = DbhP_7,32.50 //
children.translated_text: always impelled by my power, imagined in me, O king. (Dg 2.50)

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s>—thus the thirty-second chapter of the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devī Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.

children.text:
atha tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the third chapter—the seventh book, now the thirty-third chapter.
The <s>Devī</s> said:
The entire world of moving and non-moving beings is fashioned by my power of <s>Māyā</s>;

children.text: sāpi mattaḥ pṛthaṅmāyā nāstyeva paramārthataḥ // Dg_3.1 = DbhP_7,33.1 //
children.translated_text: and that <s>Māyā</s> too, separate from me, does not truly exist in the ultimate sense. (Dg 3.1)
From the standpoint of conventional perception, she is known as <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>Māyā</s>;

children.text: tattvadṛṣṭyā tu nāstyeva tattvamevāsti kevalam // Dg_3.2 = DbhP_7,33.2 //
children.translated_text: but from the standpoint of truth, she does not exist—the truth alone exists. (Dg 3.2)
I, having created this entire world, enter into it,
accompanied by <s>Māyā</s>, <s>karma</s>, and the rest, O Mountain, preceded by <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath). (Dg 3.3)
Because otherwise the passage to other worlds would not be possible,

children.text: yathā yathā bhavantyeva māyābhedāstathā tathā // Dg_3.4 = DbhP_7,33.4 //
children.translated_text: as there are divisions of <s>Māyā</s>, just so [the entry occurs]. (Dg 3.4)
Through the difference of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), I appear divided, like the space in pots and the like.
Just as the sun, always illuminating high and low objects alike, (Dg 3.5)

children.text: na duṣyati tathaivāhaṃ doṣairliptā kadāpi na /
children.translated_text: is not tainted—so too I am never tainted by faults.
Others superimpose upon me the agency of intellect and the rest, (Dg 3.6)

children.text: vadanti cātmā karmeti vimūḍhā na subuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: and speak deludedly, saying "the self acts through <s>karma</s>"—they are not of sound understanding.
Just as through the division of ignorance and through the division of <s>Māyā</s>, (Dg 3.7)
the distinction between <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord) is merely imagined by <s>Māy��</s> alone,
just as the distinction between the space in a pot and the great space is imagined— (Dg 3.8)
so too the difference between <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) and <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self) is imagined.

children.text: yathā jīvabahūtvaṃ ca māyayaiva na ca svataḥ // Dg_3.9 = DbhP_7,33.9 //
children.translated_text: Just as the multiplicity of <s>jīvas</s> is through <s>Māyā</s> alone and not intrinsic, (Dg 3.9)
so too the multiplicity of <s>Īśvaras</s> is through <s>Māyā</s> and not by own nature.
<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), differentiated by the differences of impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of the aggregate of body, senses, and the rest, (Dg 3.10)
is declared to be the cause of the differentiation of <s>jīvas</s>, and no other.

children.text: guṇānāṃ vāsanābhedabheditā yā dharādhara // Dg_3.11 = DbhP_7,33.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, differentiated by the differences of impressions of the <s>guṇas</s>, O supporter of the earth, (Dg 3.11)
is the cause of the differentiation of the Lord, and never any other.

children.text: mayi sarvamidaṃ protamotaṃ ca dharaṇīdhara // Dg_3.12 = DbhP_7,33.12 //
children.translated_text: In me all this is woven lengthwise and crosswise, O bearer of the earth. (Dg 3.12)
I am <s>Īśvara</s>, I am the thread-self (<s>Sūtrātman</s>), I am the cosmic self (<s>Virāṭ</s>);

children.text: brahmāhaṃ viṣṇurudrau ca gaurī brāhmī ca vaiṣṇāvī // Dg_3.13 = DbhP_7,33.13 //
children.translated_text: I am <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>; I am <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>. (Dg 3.13)
I am the sun, I am the stars, and I am the lord of stars (moon);

children.text: paśupakṣisvarūpāhaṃ cāṇḍālo 'haṃ ca taskaraḥ // Dg_3.14 = DbhP_7,33.14 //
children.translated_text: I am of the form of animals and birds; I am the outcaste and the thief. (Dg 3.14)
I am the hunter, I am cruel deeds, I am good deeds, I am the great person;
I am of female, male, and neuter form—without doubt, I alone am [all this]. (Dg 3.15)
Whatever thing whatsoever, anywhere, is seen or heard,

children.text: antarbahiśca tatsarvaṃ vyāpyāhaṃ sarvadā sthitā // Dg_3.16 = DbhP_7,33.16 //
children.translated_text: within and without—pervading all of that, I abide always. (Dg 3.16)

children.text: na tadasti mayā tyaktaṃ vastu kiñciccarācaram /
children.translated_text: There is nothing, moving or non-moving, that is abandoned by me;

children.text: yadyasti cettacchūnyaṃ syādvandhyāputropamaṃ hi tat // Dg_3.17 = DbhP_7,33.17 //
children.translated_text: if anything were [without me], it would be empty—like the son of a barren woman. (Dg 3.17)
Just as a single rope appears in various forms as a snake, a garland, and the like,

children.text: tathaiveśādirūpeṇa bhāmyahaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ // Dg_3.18 = DbhP_7,33.18 //
children.translated_text: so too I appear in the form of <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest—there is no doubt in this. (Dg 3.18)
What is imagined does not shine apart from the substratum;
therefore, only through my reality does this [world] possess existence—not otherwise. (Dg 3.19)
<s>Himālaya</s> said:
As you speak, O goddess of the gods, of this cosmic (<s>samaṣṭi</s>) form—

children.text: tathaiva draṣṭumicchāmi yadi devi kṛpā mayi // Dg_3.20 = DbhP_7,33.20 //
children.translated_text: I wish to behold it, if, O <s>Devī</s>, you have compassion upon me. (Dg 3.20)
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve devāḥ saviṣṇavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard his words, all the gods, including <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
rejoiced with delighted hearts, honoring his speech. (Dg 3.21)
Then the auspicious <s>Devī</s>, knowing the wish of the gods, she who fulfills the desires of her devotees,
revealed her own form, she who fulfills the desires of devotees. (Dg 3.22)
They beheld the <s>Virāṭ</s> form of the Great Goddess, supreme beyond the supreme—

children.text: dyaurmastakaṃ bhavedyasya candramūryau ca cakṣuṣī // Dg_3.23 = DbhP_7,33.23 //
children.translated_text: the sky was her head, the moon and sun were her eyes; (Dg 3.23)

children.text: diśaḥ śrotre vaco devāḥ prāṇo vāyuḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: the directions were her ears, the gods were her speech; <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is declared as her breath;

children.text: viśvaṃ hṛdayamityāhuḥ pṛthivī jaghanaṃ smṛtam // Dg_3.24 = DbhP_7,33.24 //
children.translated_text: the universe, they say, is her heart; the earth is her loins. (Dg 3.24)
The firmament is the hollow of her navel; the circle of luminaries is her chest;

children.text: maharlokastu grīvā syājjanoloko mukhaṃ smṛtam // Dg_3.25 = DbhP_7,33.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Maharloka</s> is the neck; <s>Janaloka</s> is regarded as the face.
<s>Tapoloka</s> is the forehead, situated below <s>Satyaloka</s>;

children.text: indrādayo bāhavaḥ syuḥ śabdaḥ śrotraṃ maheśituḥ // Dg_3.26 = DbhP_7,33.26 //
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and the other [gods] are the arms; sound is the ear of the Great Goddess.

children.text: nāsatyadasrau nāse sto gandho ghrāṇaṃ smṛtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The two <s>Nāsatyas</s> (<s>Aśvins</s>) are the two nostrils; smell is said to be the nose;

children.text: mukhamagniḥ samākhyāto divārātrī ca pakṣmaṇī // Dg_3.27 = DbhP_7,33.27 //
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> (fire) is declared to be the mouth; day and night are the two eyelashes.
The abode of <s>Brahmā</s> is the space between the brows; the waters are declared to be the palate;

children.text: raso jihvā samākhyātā yamo daṃṣṭrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Dg_3.28 = DbhP_7,33.28 //
children.translated_text: Taste is declared to be the tongue; <s>Yama</s> is declared to be the fangs.

children.text: dantāḥ snehakalā yasya hāso māyā prakīrtitā /
children.translated_text: The teeth are her digits of affection; laughter is declared to be <s>māyā</s> (illusion);
Creation is the casting of her sidelong glance; modesty is the upper lip of the Great Goddess.
Greed is her lower lip; the path of <s>dharma</s> is the region of her back;

children.text: prajāpatiśca meḍhraṃ syādyaḥ sraṣṭā jagatītale // Dg_3.30 = DbhP_7,33.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, the creator upon the surface of the earth, is her generative organ.
The oceans are her belly; the mountains are the bones of the Goddess, the Great Ruler;

children.text: nadyo nāḍyaḥ samākhyātā vṛkṣāḥ keśaḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Dg_3.31 = DbhP_7,33.31 //
children.translated_text: The rivers are declared to be her veins; the trees are declared to be her hair.
Childhood, youth, and old age are the stages of her excellent course;

children.text: balāhakāstu keśāḥ syuḥ sandhye te vāsasī vibho // Dg_3.32 = DbhP_7,33.32 //
children.translated_text: The clouds are her hair; the two twilights are her garments, O Lord.
O King, the moon is regarded as the mind of <s>Śrī Jagadambā</s> (Mother of the Universe);

children.text: vijñānaśaktistu harī rudro 'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ smṛtam // Dg_3.33 = DbhP_7,33.33 //
children.translated_text: The power of discernment is <s>Hari</s>; <s>Rudra</s> is regarded as the inner faculty.

children.text: aśvā hi jātayaḥ sarvāḥ śroṇideśe sthitā vibhoḥ /
children.translated_text: Horses and all species are situated in the region of her hips;
The nether worlds beginning with <s>Atala</s> are situated in the region below her waist.
The foremost of the gods beheld such a great form,

children.text: jvālāmālāsahasrāḍhyaṃ lelihānaṃ ca jihvayā // Dg_3.35 = DbhP_7,33.35 //
children.translated_text: Resplendent with thousands of garlands of flames, licking with her tongue,
Making a crunching sound with her fangs, vomiting fire from her eyes,

children.text: nānāyudhadharaṃ vīraṃ brahmakṣatraudanaṃ ca yat // Dg_3.36 = DbhP_7,33.36 //
children.translated_text: Bearing various weapons, heroic, for whom <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s> are food,
Having a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet,
Radiant as ten million suns, with the brilliance of ten million lightning bolts,
Terrifying, supremely dreadful, causing fear in the hearts and eyes—

children.text: dadṛśuste surāḥ sarve hāhākāraṃ ca cakrire // Dg_3.38 = DbhP_7,33.38 //
children.translated_text: All the gods beheld [her] and cried out 'Alas! Alas!'
Their hearts trembling, they fell into an irresistible swoon;

children.text: smaraṇaṃ ca gataṃ teṣāṃ jagadambeyamityapi // Dg_3.39 = DbhP_7,33.39 //
children.translated_text: Even the memory that she was <s>Jagadambā</s> (Mother of the Universe) left them.

children.text: atha te ye sthitā vedāścaturdikṣu mahāvibhoḥ /
children.translated_text: Then those <s>Vedas</s> who were stationed in the four directions of the Great Lord
Revived the most fiercely swooning gods from their fainting.

children.text: atha te dhairyamālambya labdhvā ca śrutimuttamām /
children.translated_text: Then, gathering their courage and having received the supreme teaching,
With eyes filled with tears of love and throats choked,
With voices stammering with sobs, they began to praise her.
The gods said:

children.text: uparādhaṃ kṣamasvāmba pāhi dīnāṃstvadudbhavān // Dg_3.42 = DbhP_7,33.42 //
children.translated_text: "Forgive our offense, O Mother! Protect your wretched children, born from you!
Withdraw your anger, O Goddess of Gods! We are frightened by the sight of this form.

children.text: kā te stutiḥ prakartavyā pāmarairnirjarairiha // Dg_3.43 = DbhP_7,33.43 //
children.translated_text: What praise can be offered by such wretched immortals as us?
Even to herself, her own power is unknowable in its full extent;

children.text: tadarvāgjāyamānānāṃ kathaṃ sa viṣayo bhavet // Dg_3.44 = DbhP_7,33.44 //
children.translated_text: How then could it be within the reach of those born after her?
Salutation to you, O Sovereign of the Worlds! Salutation to you, O embodiment of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ)!
O you who are established in all <s>Vedānta</s>, salutation to the embodiment of <s>Hrīṃ</s>!
From whom <s>Agni</s> (fire) was born, from whom the sun and moon,

children.text: yasmādoṣadhayaḥ sarvāstasmai sarvātmane namaḥ // Dg_3.46 = DbhP_7,33.46 //
children.translated_text: From whom all herbs—salutation to that Self of all!

children.text: yasmācca devāḥ sambhūtāḥ sādhyāḥpakṣiṇa eva ca /
children.translated_text: From whom the gods were born, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, birds,

children.text: paśavaśca manuṣyāśca tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ // Dg_3.47 = DbhP_7,33.47 //
children.translated_text: Animals, and humans—salutation to that Self of all!

children.text: prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaḥ śraddhā ṛtaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, rice and barley, <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order),

children.text: brahmacaryaṃ vidhiścaiva yasmāttasmai namo namaḥ // Dg_3.48 = DbhP_7,33.48 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and ritual law—from whom [all these arise], salutation, salutation!

children.text: sapta prāṇārciṣo yasmātsamidhaḥ sapta eva ca /
children.translated_text: From whom the seven <s>prāṇa</s>-flames, the seven fuels,

children.text: homāḥ sapta tathā lokāstasmai sarvātmane namaḥ // Dg_3.49 = DbhP_7,33.49 //
children.translated_text: The seven oblations, and likewise the [seven] worlds—salutation to that Self of all!
From whom the oceans, mountains, and rivers flow forth,

children.text: yasmādoṣadhayaḥ sarvā rasāstasmai namo namaḥ // Dg_3.50 = DbhP_7,33.50 //
children.translated_text: From whom all herbs and their essences—salutation, salutation!
From whom sacrifice was born, initiation, the sacrificial post, and the ritual fees,

children.text: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ // Dg_3.51 = DbhP_7,33.51 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> [verses]—salutation to that Self of all!
Salutation before you, behind you, salutation on both your sides,

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ caturdikṣu mātarbhūyo namo namaḥ // Dg_3.52 = DbhP_7,33.52 //
children.translated_text: Below, above, in the four directions—O Mother, salutation again and again!
Withdraw, O Goddess of Gods, this supernatural form;

children.text: tadeva darśayāsmākaṃ rūpaṃ sundarasundaram // Dg_3.53 = DbhP_7,33.53 //
children.translated_text: Show us instead that form which is supremely beautiful."
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Having seen the frightened gods, <s>Jagadambā</s>, ocean of compassion,

children.text: saṃhṛtya rūpaṃ ghoraṃ taddarśayāmāsa sundaram // Dg_3.54 = DbhP_7,33.54 //
children.translated_text: Withdrew that terrible form and displayed her beautiful one—
Holding the noose, the goad, and [the gestures of] boon-granting and fearlessness, soft in all her limbs,
With eyes full of compassion and a lotus-face bearing a gentle smile.
Having seen that beautiful form, then free from fear,
With peaceful minds they bowed down, their voices stammering with joy.

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Devī Gītā</s>.
Thus the thirty-third chapter in the seventh book of the <s>Śrī Devī Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Devī Gītā</s>.

children.text:
atha caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now the fourth chapter.
Seventh Book.
Now the thirty-fourth chapter.
The Blessed Goddess said:

children.text: kva yūyaṃ mandabhāgyā vai kvedaṃ rūpaṃ mahādbhutam /
children.translated_text: "How unfortunate you are, and how wondrous is this form!

children.text: tathāpi bhaktavātsalyādīdṛśaṃ darśitaṃ mayā // Dg_4.1 = DbhP_7,34.1 //
children.translated_text: Yet out of affection for my devotees, I have shown it to you.
Not by study of the <s>Vedas</s>, nor by <s>yoga</s>, nor by gifts, austerity, or worship

children.text: rūpaṃ draṣṭum idaṃ śakyaṃ kevalaṃ matkṛpāṃ vinā // Dg_4.2 = DbhP_7,34.2 //
children.translated_text: Can this form be seen—only through my grace alone.
Hear now the main topic, O best of kings: the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), here among the living,

children.text: upādhiyogāt samprāptaḥ kartṛtvādikam apyuta // Dg_4.3 = DbhP_7,34.3 //
children.translated_text: Through connection with <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts), has acquired agency and the like.
He performs various actions, which are the sole causes of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>;

children.text: nānā yonīstataḥ prāpya sukhaduḥkhaiśca yujyate // Dg_4.4 = DbhP_7,34.4 //
children.translated_text: Then, obtaining various wombs, he is joined with pleasure and pain.
Again, due to the force of those <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions), ever engaged in various actions,

children.text: nānā dehān samāpnoti sukhaduḥkhaiśca yujyate // Dg_4.5 = DbhP_7,34.5 //
children.translated_text: He obtains various bodies and is joined with pleasure and pain.
Like a waterwheel, there is never any rest for him;

children.text: ajñānam eva mūlaṃ syāt tataḥ kāmaḥ kriyāstataḥ // Dg_4.6 = DbhP_7,34.6 //
children.translated_text: Ignorance alone is the root, from that comes desire, and from that, actions.
Therefore a person should strive diligently for the destruction of ignorance;

children.text: etaddhi janmasāphalyaṃ yadajñānasya nāśanam // Dg_4.7 = DbhP_7,34.7 //
children.translated_text: For this indeed is the fruition of birth—the destruction of ignorance.
The fulfillment of the goals of human life and even the state of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living)—

children.text: ajñānanāśane śaktā vidyaiva tu paṭīyasī // Dg_4.8 = DbhP_7,34.8 //
children.translated_text: Only <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is most capable of destroying ignorance.
Neither <s>karma</s> (action), nor what arises from it, nor <s>upāsanā</s> (worship) [can destroy ignorance], because there is no opposition [between them and ignorance]. O Mountain,

children.text: pratyutāśājñānanāśe karmaṇā naiva bhāvyatām // Dg_4.9 = DbhP_7,34.9 //
children.translated_text: Rather, one should not expect the destruction of ignorance through <s>karma</s> at all.
Actions bring misfortune again and again;

children.text: tato rāgastato doṣastato 'nartho mahānbhavet // Dg_4.10 = DbhP_7,34.10 //
children.translated_text: From them arises attachment, from that arises fault, and from that a great calamity results.
Therefore, with every effort a person should cultivate knowledge,
While still performing actions here—thus <s>karma</s> too is necessary.

children.text: jñānādeva hi kaivalyam ataḥ syāt tatsamuccayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation) comes from knowledge alone; therefore there should be a combination of the two;

children.text: sahāyatāṃ vrajet karma jñānasya hitakāri ca // Dg_4.12 = DbhP_7,34.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> should serve as an auxiliary, beneficial to knowledge.
Some say this, but due to their mutual opposition, it is not possible;
From knowledge comes the cutting of the heart's knot; from the heart's knot arises <s>karma</s>.

children.text: yaugapadyaṃ na sambhāvyaṃ virodhāt tu tatastayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Their simultaneity is not conceivable, because of their opposition;

children.text: tamaḥ prakāśayoryadvadyaugapadyaṃ na sambhavi // Dg_4.14 = DbhP_7,34.14 //
children.translated_text: Just as the simultaneity of darkness and light is not possible.
Therefore, all Vedic <s>karmas</s>, O great-minded one,

children.text: cittaśuddhyantam eva syustāni kuryāt prayatnataḥ // Dg_4.15 = DbhP_7,34.15 //
children.translated_text: Extend only up to the purification of the mind; one should perform them with effort.
<s>Śama</s> (tranquility), <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), <s>titikṣā</s> (forbearance), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and the arising of <s>sattva</s>—

children.text: tāvat paryantam eva syuḥ karmāṇi na tataḥ param // Dg_4.16 = DbhP_7,34.16 //
children.translated_text: Actions extend only up to that point and no further.
After that, having renounced, the self-possessed one should take refuge in a <s>guru</s>,

children.text: śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭhaṃ ca bhaktyā nirvyājayā punaḥ // Dg_4.17 = DbhP_7,34.17 //
children.translated_text: One who is learned in scripture and established in <s>Brahman</s>, with sincere devotion.
One should always listen to <s>Vedānta</s> teachings, thus, without laziness;

children.text: tat tvam asyādi vākyasya nityam arthaṃ vicārayet // Dg_4.18 = DbhP_7,34.18 //
children.translated_text: One should constantly contemplate the meaning of the <s>mahāvākyas</s> such as '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art).

children.text: tat tvam asyādi vākyaṃ tu jīvabrahmaikyabodhakam /
children.translated_text: The sentence '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' and similar <s>mahāvākyas</s> reveal the identity of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: aikye jñāte nirbhayastu madrūpo hi prajāyate // Dg_4.19 = DbhP_7,34.19 //
children.translated_text: When this identity is known, one becomes fearless and assumes my own form.
First comes the understanding of the word-meanings, then the understanding of the sentence-meaning;

children.text: tat padasya ca vākyārtho gire 'haṃ parikīrtitaḥ // Dg_4.20 = DbhP_7,34.20 //
children.translated_text: The sentence-meaning of the word '<s>Tat</s>' (That), O Mountain, is declared to be myself.

children.text: tvaṃ padasya ca vākyārtho jīva eva na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sentence-meaning of the word '<s>Tvam</s>' (Thou) is the <s>jīva</s> (individual self), without doubt;

children.text: ubhayor aikyam asinā padena procyate budhaiḥ // Dg_4.21 = DbhP_7,34.21 //
children.translated_text: The identity of the two is expressed by the wise through the word '<s>Asi</s>' (art).
Since the literal meanings of the two are contradictory, their identity cannot be established;

children.text: lakṣaṇātaḥ prakartavyā tattvamoḥ śrutisaṃsthayoḥ // Dg_4.22 = DbhP_7,34.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) must be applied to '<s>Tat</s>' and '<s>Tvam</s>' as they stand in the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).
Pure consciousness alone is the indicated meaning of both; thus their identity is possible;

children.text: tayoraikyaṃ tathā jñātvā svābhedenādvayo bhavet // Dg_4.23 = DbhP_7,34.23 //
children.translated_text: Having thus known their identity, one becomes non-dual through identity with the Self.

children.text: devadattaḥ sa evāyam iti vallakṣaṇā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'This is that same <s>Devadatta</s>'—this is how <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is understood;

children.text: sthūlādi deharahito brahma sampadyate naraḥ // Dg_4.24 = DbhP_7,34.24 //
children.translated_text: Freed from the gross body and the rest, a person attains <s>Brahman</s>.
The gross body is produced from the five great elements that have undergone <s>pañcīkaraṇa</s> (quintuplication);
It is the abode of enjoyment, conjoined with old age, disease, and all <s>karmas</s>.
This [body] appears as if real, [but] is clearly false because it is made of <s>māyā</s>;

children.text: so 'yaṃ sthūla upādhiḥ syādātmano me nageśvara // Dg_4.26 = DbhP_7,34.26 //
children.translated_text: This gross body is the [first] <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct) of the Self, O Lord of Mountains.
Endowed with the five organs of knowledge and the five organs of action, conjoined with the five <s>prāṇas</s>,

children.text: manobuddhiyutaṃ caitat sūkṣmaṃ tatkavayo viduḥ // Dg_4.27 = DbhP_7,34.27 //
children.translated_text: Together with <s>manas</s> (mind) and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect)—this the wise know as the subtle [body].
Arising from the un-quintupled elements, this is the subtle body of the Self;

children.text: dvitīyo 'yam upādhiḥ syāt sukhāderavabodhakaḥ // Dg_4.28 = DbhP_7,34.28 //
children.translated_text: This is the second <s>upādhi</s>, the perceiver of pleasure and the rest.
Beginningless and indescribable, this ignorance is the third

children.text: deho 'yam ātmano bhāti kāraṇātmā nageśvara // Dg_4.29 = DbhP_7,34.29 //
children.translated_text: Body of the Self, known as the causal body, O Lord of Mountains.
When the <s>upādhis</s> dissolve, the Self alone remains;

children.text: dehatraye pañcakośā antaḥsthāḥ santi sarvadā // Dg_4.30 = DbhP_7,34.30 //
children.translated_text: Within the three bodies, the five <s>kośas</s> (sheaths) always abide.
When the five <s>kośas</s> are relinquished, <s>Brahman</s>, the 'tail' [of the bliss-sheath], is obtained;

children.text: neti neti iti ādivākyair mama rūpaṃ yaducyate // Dg_4.31 = DbhP_7,34.31 //
children.translated_text: By the <s>śruti</s> statements beginning with '<s>Neti neti</s>' (Not this, not this), my true form is expressed.

children.text: na jāyate mriyate tat kadācinnāyaṃ bhūtvā na babhūva kaścit /
children.translated_text: It is never born, nor does it die; having been, it never ceases to be;

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre // Dg_4.32 = DbhP_7,34.32 //
children.translated_text: Unborn, eternal, everlasting, primeval—it is not slain when the body is slain.
If the slayer thinks he slays, if the slain thinks he is slain—

children.text: ubhau tau na vijānītau nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate // Dg_4.33 = DbhP_7,34.33 //
children.translated_text: Both of them do not understand: this one neither slays nor is slain.

children.text: aṇoraṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmāsya jantornihito guhāyām /
children.translated_text: Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the Self is hidden in the cave of the heart of this being;

children.text: tam akratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuḥ prasādān mahimānam asya // Dg_4.34 = DbhP_7,34.34 //
children.translated_text: One who is free from desire beholds it, free from sorrow, through the grace of the Creator—its majesty.

children.text: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu /
children.translated_text: Know the Self as the rider in the chariot, and the body as the chariot itself;

children.text: buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca // Dg_4.35 = DbhP_7,34.35 //
children.translated_text: Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.

children.text: indriyāṇi hayān āhur viṣayāṃs teṣu gocarān /
children.translated_text: The senses, they say, are the horses; the sense-objects are their paths;
The Self, conjoined with the senses and the mind, is called the enjoyer, say the wise.
But one who is without knowledge, always unmindful and impure—

children.text: na tatpadam avāpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati // Dg_4.37 = DbhP_7,34.37 //
children.translated_text: He does not reach that goal, and enters the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: yastu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who possesses discernment, is always mindful and pure—

children.text: sa tu tatpadam āpnoti yasmād bhūyo na jāyate // Dg_4.38 = DbhP_7,34.38 //
children.translated_text: He indeed reaches that goal from which he is not born again.
The person who has discernment as his charioteer and the mind as his reins—

children.text: so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti madīyaṃ yatparaṃ padam // Dg_4.39 = DbhP_7,34.39 //
children.translated_text: He reaches the end of the journey, which is my supreme abode.

children.text: itthaṃ śrutyā ca matyā ca niścityātmānam ātmanā /
children.translated_text: Thus, having ascertained the Self through <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>mati</s> (reason),
One should meditate on me as the Self through <s>nididhyāsana</s> (contemplation).
Before the practice of <s>yoga</s>, one should meditate on the three syllables within oneself,
For the purpose of meditating on the <s>Devīpraṇava</s> (the Goddess's Oṃ), on the <s>mantra</s> and its referent.
The syllable 'Ha' is the gross body; the syllable 'Ra' is the subtle body;

children.text: īkāraḥ kāraṇātmāsau hrīṅkāro 'haṃ turīyakam // Dg_4.42 = DbhP_7,34.42 //
children.translated_text: The <s>ī-kāra</s> is the causal self; the <s>hrīṃ-kāra</s> is the fourth state, which is myself.
Thus, in the cosmic body too, having known the triad of <s>bījas</s> (seed-syllables) in sequence,
the wise person should meditate on the oneness of the cosmic and the individual.
Before the time of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), having meditated thus with care,

children.text: tato dhyāyennilīnākṣo devīṃ māṃ jagadīśvarīm // Dg_4.44 = DbhP_7,34.44 //
children.translated_text: one should then meditate with senses withdrawn on the <s>Devī</s>, on me, the sovereign of the universe.
Having made the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> (in-breath and out-breath) equal, moving within the nostrils,
free from longing for sense objects, free from faults, free from jealousy,

children.text: bhaktyā nirvyājayā yukto guhāyāṃ niḥsvane sthale /
children.translated_text: endowed with sincere <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), in a cave, in a silent place,

children.text: hakāram viśvam ātmānaṃ rakāre pravilāpayet // Dg_4.46 = DbhP_7,34.46 //
children.translated_text: one should dissolve the <s>ha-kāra</s>, which is the self of the universe, into the <s>ra-kāra</s>.
One should dissolve the <s>ra-kāra</s>, the luminous deity, into the <s>ī-kāra</s>;

children.text: īkāraṃ prājñam ātmānaṃ hrīṅkāre pravilāpayet // Dg_4.47 = DbhP_7,34.47 //
children.translated_text: one should dissolve the <s>ī-kāra</s>, the self of deep sleep, into the <s>hrīṃ-kāra</s>.
Devoid of the relation of word and meaning, free from the state of duality,

children.text: akhaṇḍaṃ saccidānandaṃ bhāvayet tacchikhāntare // Dg_4.48 = DbhP_7,34.48 //
children.translated_text: one should meditate on the undivided <s>saccidānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss) within the tip of that flame.

children.text: iti dhyānena māṃ rājan sākṣātkṛtya narottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, by meditation, having directly realized me, the best of men

children.text: madrūpa eva bhavati dvayorapyekatā yataḥ // Dg_4.49 = DbhP_7,34.49 //
children.translated_text: becomes identical with my form, since there is oneness of the two.
Having seen me, the Supreme Self, beyond the highest, through this method of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: ajñānasya sakāryasya tat kṣaṇo nāśako bhavet // Dg_4.50 = DbhP_7,34.50 //
children.translated_text: that very moment becomes the destroyer of ignorance along with its effects.

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.

children.text:
atha pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now begins the fifth chapter.
Seventh Book.
Now the thirty-fifth chapter.
<s>Himālaya</s> said:
O great sovereign goddess, teach me <s>yoga</s> together with its limbs, which bestows realization,

children.text: kṛtena yena yogyo 'haṃ bhaveyaṃ tattvadarśane // Dg_5.1 = DbhP_7,35.1 //
children.translated_text: by the practice of which I may become fit for the vision of the ultimate reality.
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: na yogo nabhasaḥ pṛṣṭhe na bhūmau na rasātale /
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is not on the surface of the sky, not on the earth, not in the netherworld;

children.text: aikyaṃ jīvātmanor āhur yogaṃ yogaviśāradāḥ // Dg_5.2 = DbhP_7,35.2 //
children.translated_text: those versed in <s>yoga</s> call <s>yoga</s> the union of the individual self and the supreme self.
Six obstacles are declared to be hindrances to <s>yoga</s>, O sinless one:
desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and jealousy.
By the limbs of <s>yoga</s> alone, having destroyed these, <s>yogins</s> attain <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: yamaṃ niyamamāsanaprāṇāyāmau tataḥ param // Dg_5.4 = DbhP_7,35.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), <s>āsana</s> (postures), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), and then
<s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) together with <s>samādhi</s> (absorption)—
these eight limbs are declared for <s>yogins</s> in the practice of <s>yoga</s>.
<s>Ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing), <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), <s>dayā</s> (compassion), <s>ārjava</s> (straightforwardness),

children.text: kṣamā dhṛtirmitāhāraḥ śaucaṃ ceti yamā daśa // Dg_5.6 = DbhP_7,35.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>kṣamā</s> (patience), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>mitāhāra</s> (moderate diet), and <s>śauca</s> (purity)—these are the ten <s>yamas</s>.

children.text: tapaḥ santoṣa āstikyaṃ dānaṃ devasya pūjanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tapas</s> (austerity), <s>santoṣa</s> (contentment), <s>āstikya</s> (faith in the scriptures), <s>dāna</s> (charity), worship of the deity,

children.text: siddhāntaśravaṇaṃ caiva hrīrmatiśca japo hutam // Dg_5.7 = DbhP_7,35.7 //
children.translated_text: listening to the established doctrines, <s>hrī</s> (modesty), <s>mati</s> (wisdom), <s>japa</s> (recitation), and <s>huta</s> (fire-offering)—
these ten <s>niyamas</s> have been declared by me, O lord of mountains.

children.text: padmāsanaṃ svastikaṃ ca bhadraṃ vajrāsanaṃ tathā // Dg_5.8 = DbhP_7,35.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), <s>svastika</s>, <s>bhadra</s> (auspicious posture), <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond posture),
and <s>vīrāsana</s> (hero posture)—these are declared as the five principal <s>āsanas</s> in order.

children.text: ūrvorupari vinyasya samyakpādatale śubhe // Dg_5.9 = DbhP_7,35.9 //
children.translated_text: Placing both beautiful soles of the feet properly upon the thighs,
one should bind the big toes with the hands alternately;

children.text: padmāsanamiti proktaṃ yogināṃ hṛdayaṅgamam // Dg_5.10 = DbhP_7,35.10 //
children.translated_text: this is called <s>padmāsana</s>, dear to the hearts of <s>yogins</s>.
Placing the beautiful soles of the feet properly between the knees and thighs,

children.text: kṛjukāyo viśedyogī svastikaṃ tatpracakṣate // Dg_5.11 = DbhP_7,35.11 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s> should sit with body erect; this they call <s>svastika</s>.
Placing both ankles firmly beside the perineum,

children.text: vṛṣaṇādhaḥ pādapārṣṇī pārṣṇibhyāṃ paribandhayet // Dg_5.12 = DbhP_7,35.12 //
children.translated_text: one should bind the heels below the scrotum with both heels;
this is called <s>bhadrāsana</s>, honored by <s>yogins</s>.

children.text: urvoḥ pādau kramānnyasya jānvoḥ pratyaṅmukhāṅgulī // Dg_5.13 = DbhP_7,35.13 //
children.translated_text: Placing the feet in order upon the thighs, with toes facing the knees,
one should position the hands—this is declared as the supreme <s>vajrāsana</s>.

children.text: ekaṃ pādamadhaḥ kṛtvā vinyasyoruṃ tathottare // Dg_5.14 = DbhP_7,35.14 //
children.translated_text: Placing one foot below and extending the thigh upon the other,
the <s>yogin</s> should sit with body erect; this is called <s>vīrāsana</s>.

children.text: iḍayākarṣayet vāyuṃ bāhyaṃ ṣoḍaśamātrayā // Dg_5.15 = DbhP_7,35.15 //
children.translated_text: One should draw in the external air through the <s>iḍā</s> (left nostril) for sixteen measures;
the <s>yogin</s> should retain the filled breath for sixty-four measures,
properly through the middle of the <s>suṣumnā</s>, and slowly for thirty-two measures
one should exhale through the <s>piṅgalā</s> <s>nāḍī</s> (right channel)—the one most versed in <s>yoga</s>.
Those learned in the <s>yoga-śāstra</s> (science of yoga) call this <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
Again and again, in sequence, one should practice this external exercise;

children.text: mātrāvṛddhiḥ krameṇaiva samyagdvādaśa ṣoḍaśa // Dg_5.18 = DbhP_7,35.18 //
children.translated_text: the increase of measures should be gradual—properly twelve, then sixteen.
When accompanied by <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and the like, the wise call it <s>sagarbha</s> (with seed);

children.text: tadapetaṃ vigarbhaṃ ca prāṇāyāmaṃ pare viduḥ // Dg_5.19 = DbhP_7,35.19 //
children.translated_text: without these, others know it as <s>vigarbha</s> (seedless) <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
For one who practices gradually, perspiration arising in the body is the lowest stage;

children.text: madhyamaḥ kampasaṃyukto bhūmityāgaḥ paro mataḥ // Dg_5.20 = DbhP_7,35.20 //
children.translated_text: the middle stage is accompanied by trembling; the highest is considered to be rising from the ground.
The attainment of the qualities of the highest stage is desired through practice.

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ vicaratāṃ viṣayeṣu nirargalam // Dg_5.21 = DbhP_7,35.21 //
children.translated_text: The forcible withdrawal of the senses that wander unrestrained among sense objects
is called <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal).
At the big toe, ankle, knee, root of the thigh, <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root center), genitals, navel,
heart, throat, the region of the neck, the uvula, then the nose,

children.text: bhrūmadhye mastake mūrdhni dvādaśānte yathāvidhi // Dg_5.23 = DbhP_7,35.23 //
children.translated_text: between the eyebrows, at the head, at the crown, and at the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (the point twelve finger-widths above)—in proper order,
the holding of the <s>prāṇa</s> breath is called <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).
With a collected mind, dwelling within consciousness,
<s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is here called the meditation on one's chosen deities within the self.
The constant contemplation of the equality of the individual self and the supreme self
is called <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) by the sages. Thus has been declared the nature of the eight limbs.

children.text: idānīṃ kathaye te 'haṃ mantrayogamanuttamam // Dg_5.26 = DbhP_7,35.26 //
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell you the supreme <s>mantrayoga</s> (yoga of mantras).
The universe has been called the body, O mountain, composed of the five elements,
with the radiance of moon, sun, and fire, having the form of the unity of <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Brahman</s>.
Three and a half <s>koṭis</s> (millions) of <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) are said to exist in the body;

children.text: tāsu mukhyā daśa proktāstābhyastisro vyavasthitāḥ // Dg_5.28 = DbhP_7,35.28 //
children.translated_text: among them, ten are declared as principal; of those, three are established as paramount.

children.text: iḍā vāme sthitā nāḍī śubhrā tu candrarūpiṇī // Dg_5.29 = DbhP_7,35.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s> is the <s>nāḍī</s> situated on the left, luminous, having the form of the moon.
Chief among them, in the spinal column, having the forms of moon, sun, and fire at its summit—
That <s>nāḍī</s> has the form of <s>Śakti</s> (power), being truly the embodiment of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar);

children.text: dakṣiṇe yā piṅgalākhyā puṃrūpā sūryavigrahā // Dg_5.30 = DbhP_7,35.30 //
children.translated_text: on the right is the one called <s>Piṅgalā</s>, masculine in nature, the embodiment of the sun.
Consisting entirely of radiance, <s>Suṣumnā</s> has the form of fire;

children.text: tasyā madhye vicitrākhye icchājñānakriyātmakam // Dg_5.31 = DbhP_7,35.31 //
children.translated_text: in its middle, in the one called <s>Citrā</s>, consisting of will, knowledge, and action,
in the middle is the <s>Svayambhū-liṅga</s>, radiant as ten million suns.

children.text: tadūrdhvaṃ māyābījaṃ tu harātmā bindunādakam // Dg_5.32 = DbhP_7,35.32 //
children.translated_text: Above that is the <s>māyā-bīja</s> (seed of illusion), the self of <s>Hara</s>, with <s>bindu</s> (dot) and <s>nāda</s> (sound).
Above that, in the form of a flame, is <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, of red complexion,

children.text: devyātmikā tu sā proktā madabhinnā nagādhipa // Dg_5.33 = DbhP_7,35.33 //
children.translated_text: declared to be of the nature of the <s>Devī</s>, non-different from me, O lord of mountains.
Outside of that, resembling the form of gold, with four petals ending in the syllables <s>va</s> to <s>sa</s>,

children.text: drutahemasamaprakhyaṃ padmaṃ tatra vicintayet // Dg_5.34 = DbhP_7,35.34 //
children.translated_text: one should visualize a lotus resembling molten gold.
Above that, resembling fire, with six petals, having the luster of diamond,
with the six letters from <s>ba</s> to <s>la</s>—this is the supreme <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> (one's own abode).
The root <s>ādhāra</s> (support) is hexagonal; hence it is known as <s>Mūlādhāra</s>.

children.text: svaśabdena paraṃ liṅgaṃ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ tato viduḥ // Dg_5.36 = DbhP_7,35.36 //
children.translated_text: By the word 'sva' the supreme <s>liṅga</s> is meant; hence it is known as <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>.
Above that, in the region of the navel, is <s>Maṇipūra</s> of great radiance,

children.text: meghābhaṃ vidyudābhaṃ ca bahutejomayaṃ tataḥ // Dg_5.37 = DbhP_7,35.37 //
children.translated_text: resembling a cloud, like lightning, full of abundant radiance.
That lotus, shining like a jewel, is thus called the <s>Maṇipadma</s> (jewel-lotus);
it is endowed with ten petals, bearing the letters from <s>ḍa</s> to <s>pha</s>.
That lotus is presided over by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, being the cause of the vision of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Above that is the <s>Anāhata</s> (unstruck) lotus, resembling the rising sun,
with petals bearing the letters from <s>ka</s> to <s>ṭha</s>,

children.text: tanmadhye bāṇaliṅgaṃ tu sūryāyutasamaprabham // Dg_5.40 = DbhP_7,35.40 //
children.translated_text: in the middle of which is the <s>Bāṇa-liṅga</s>, radiant as ten thousand suns.
There is seen the unstruck sound consisting of <s>śabda-brahman</s> (sonic absolute);

children.text: anāhatākhyaṃ tatpadmaṃ munibhiḥ parikīrtitam // Dg_5.41 = DbhP_7,35.41 //
children.translated_text: that lotus is called <s>Anāhata</s>, proclaimed by the sages.
That is the abode of bliss, presided over by the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person).

children.text: tadūrdhvaṃ tu viśuddhākhyaṃ dalaṃ ṣoḍaśapaṅkajam // Dg_5.42 = DbhP_7,35.42 //
children.translated_text: Above that is the one called <s>Viśuddha</s> (pure), a lotus of sixteen petals,
endowed with the sixteen vowels, of smoky color and great radiance.

children.text: viśuddhaṃ tanute yasmājjīvasya haṃsalokanāt // Dg_5.43 = DbhP_7,35.43 //
children.translated_text: It purifies the individual soul through the vision of <s>Haṃsa</s> (the divine swan);
that lotus is called <s>Viśuddha</s>, known as the space element, most wondrous.

children.text: ājñācakraṃ tadūrdhve tu ātmanādhiṣṭhitaṃ param // Dg_5.44 = DbhP_7,35.44 //
children.translated_text: Above that is the <s>Ājñā-cakra</s> (command center), presided over by the supreme Self.
There the transmission of command occurs; hence it is called <s>Ājñā</s>.

children.text: dvidalaṃ hakṣasaṃyuktaṃ padmaṃ tatsumanoharam // Dg_5.45 = DbhP_7,35.45 //
children.translated_text: That beautiful lotus has two petals, endowed with the syllables <s>ha</s> and <s>kṣa</s>.

children.text: kailāsākhyaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ tu rodhinī tu tadūrdhvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Above that is the one called <s>Kailāsa</s>, and above that is <s>Rodhinī</s>.

children.text: evaṃ tvādhāracakrāṇi proktāni tava suvrata // Dg_5.46 = DbhP_7,35.46 //
children.translated_text: Thus the supporting <s>cakras</s> (energy centers) have been declared to you, O one of good vows.
Above that is described the <s>bindu-sthāna</s> (seat of the dot), with a thousand rays.
Thus all of this has been told—the supreme path of <s>yoga</s>.
First, through the practice of <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), one should fix the mind at the <s>ādhāra</s> (base center).
Between the anus and the genitals is the <s>Śakti</s>; contracting it, one should awaken her.
Through the successive piercing of the <s>liṅgas</s>, one should cause her to reach the <s>bindu-cakra</s> (crown center).

children.text: śambhunā tāṃ parāṃ śaktimekībhūtāṃ vicintayet // Dg_5.49 = DbhP_7,35.49 //
children.translated_text: One should visualize that supreme <s>Śakti</s> united as one with <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva).
The <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) that arises there, resembling molten lac,

children.text: pāyayitvā tu tāṃ śaktiṃ māyākhyāṃ yogasiddhidam // Dg_5.50 = DbhP_7,35.50 //
children.translated_text: having given it to drink to that <s>Śakti</s> called <s>Māyā</s>, which bestows <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic perfection),
having nourished the deities of the six <s>cakras</s> with the stream of <s>amṛta</s>,

children.text: ānayettena mārgeṇa mūlādhāraṃ tataḥ sudhī // Dg_5.51 = DbhP_7,35.51 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should bring her back by that same path to the <s>Mūlādhāra</s>.
For one who practices thus every day without fail,

children.text: pūrvoktadūṣitā mantrāḥ sarve sidhyanti nānyathā // Dg_5.52 = DbhP_7,35.52 //
children.translated_text: all previously taught <s>mantras</s> become perfected; it is not otherwise.
One is freed from the bonds of existence—old age, death, suffering, and the rest.

children.text: ye guṇāḥ santi devyā me jaganmāturyathā tathā // Dg_5.53 = DbhP_7,35.53 //
children.translated_text: Whatever qualities belong to me, the <s>Devī</s>, the mother of the universe,

children.text: te guṇāḥ sādhakavare bhavantyeva na cānyathā /
children.translated_text: those very qualities arise in the best of practitioners; it is not otherwise.

children.text: ityevaṃ kathitaṃ tāta vāyudhāraṇamuttamam // Dg_5.54 = DbhP_7,35.54 //
children.translated_text: Thus has been told to you, dear one, the supreme <s>vāyudhāraṇa</s> (retention of breath).
Now hear attentively from me what is called <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).
