children.text: dikkālādyanavacchinnadevyāṃ ceto vidhāya ca // Dg_5.55 = DbhP_7,35.55 //
children.translated_text: Having fixed the mind on the <s>Devī</s>, who is unlimited by direction, time, or other constraints,
one quickly becomes identical with her, through the union of the individual self and <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: athavā samalaṃ ceto yadi kṣipraṃ na siddhyati // Dg_5.56 = DbhP_7,35.56 //
children.translated_text: Or, if the impure mind does not quickly succeed,
then the <s>yogin</s> should practice <s>yoga</s> through the method of focusing on parts.

children.text: madīyahastapādādāvaṅge tu madhure naga // Dg_5.57 = DbhP_7,35.57 //
children.translated_text: On my lovely hands, feet, and other limbs, O mountain,
the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should fix the mind; then, through mastery of successive stations,
with purified mind, one should fix the mind on the entire form.

children.text: yāvanmano layaṃ yāti devyāṃ saṃvidi parvata /
children.translated_text: Until the mind dissolves in the <s>Devī</s>, in pure consciousness, O mountain,

children.text: tāvadiṣṭamanuṃ mantrī japahomaiḥ samabhyaset // Dg_5.59 = DbhP_7,35.59 //
children.translated_text: until then the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should practice the chosen <s>mantra</s> with <s>japa</s> (recitation) and <s>homa</s> (fire offerings).
Through the practice of <s>mantras</s> and <s>yoga</s>, one becomes fit for the knowledge of the knowable.

children.text: na yogena vinā mantro na mantreṇa vinā hi saḥ // Dg_5.60 = DbhP_7,35.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is not effective without <s>mantra</s>, nor is <s>mantra</s> effective without <s>yoga</s>.
The combined practice of both is the cause of attaining <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tamaḥ parivṛte gehe ghaṭo dīpena dṛśyate // Dg_5.61 = DbhP_7,35.61 //
children.translated_text: In a room enveloped by darkness, a pot is seen by means of a lamp;
just so, the Self, concealed by <s>māyā</s> (illusion), is made perceivable by the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: iti yogavidhiḥ kṛtsnaḥ sāṅgaḥ prokto mayā 'dhunā // Dg_5.62 = DbhP_7,35.62 //
children.translated_text: Thus the complete method of <s>yoga</s>, together with its limbs, has been declared by me now.

children.text: gurūpadeśato jñeyo nānyathā śāstrakoṭibhiḥ // Dg_5.63 = DbhP_7,35.63 //
children.translated_text: It is to be known through the instruction of a <s>guru</s> (teacher), not otherwise, even through ten million scriptures.

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.
Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter in the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.

children.text:
atha ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha ṣaṭtriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now begins the sixth chapter.
Seventh Book.
Now the thirty-sixth chapter.
The <s>Devī</s> said:
Thus, with the self united through <s>yoga</s> as described above, one should meditate on me, who am of the form of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: bhaktyā nirvyājayā rājannāsane samupasthitaḥ // Dg_6.1 = DbhP_7,36.1 //
children.translated_text: with sincere <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), O king, seated on the <s>āsana</s> (seat).
That which is manifest, near at hand, moving in the cave of the heart—that great abode called by name—

children.text: atraitat sarvam arpitam ejat prāṇannimiṣacca yat // Dg_6.2 = DbhP_7,36.2 //
children.translated_text: In this, all is offered — whatever moves, breathes, and blinks.
Know this as being and non-being, the most excellent, supreme, beyond knowledge, the highest of all beings,

children.text: yadarcimadyadaṇubhyo 'ṇu ca yasmiṃllokā nihitā lokinaśca // Dg_6.3 = DbhP_7,36.3 //
children.translated_text: that which is radiant, subtler than the subtlest, in which the worlds and their inhabitants are established.
<s>Brahman</s> — that is this imperishable; it is <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), and it is speech and mind.

children.text: tadetat satyam amṛtaṃ tadveddhavyaṃ saumya viddhi // Dg_6.4 = DbhP_7,36.4 //
children.translated_text: That is truth, that is immortality — that is to be pierced. O gentle one, pierce it!
Taking up the great weapon of the <s>Upaniṣad</s> as a bow, one should fix upon it the arrow sharpened by meditation,

children.text: āyamya tadbhāvagatena cetasā lakṣyaṃ tadevākṣaraṃ saumya viddhi // Dg_6.5 = DbhP_7,36.5 //
children.translated_text: drawing it with a mind absorbed in contemplation of That — O gentle one, know that imperishable <s>Brahman</s> as the target!

children.text: praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hyātmā brahma tallakṣyam ucyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> (the syllable Om) is the bow, the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is the arrow, and <s>Brahman</s> is said to be the target.

children.text: apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravattanmayo bhavet // Dg_6.6 = DbhP_7,36.6 //
children.translated_text: It is to be pierced by one who is vigilant — like an arrow, one should become one with That.

children.text: yasmin dyauśca pṛthivī cāntarikṣam otaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiśca sarvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That in which heaven, earth, and the intermediate space are woven, along with the mind together with all the <s>Prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) —

children.text: tam evaikaṃ jānathātmānam anyā vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ // Dg_6.7 = DbhP_7,36.7 //
children.translated_text: know that alone as the one <s>Ātman</s> (Self). Abandon all other speech! This is the bridge to immortality.

children.text: arā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) converge like spokes in the hub of a chariot wheel,

children.text: sa eṣo 'ntaścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ // Dg_6.8 = DbhP_7,36.8 //
children.translated_text: that One moves within, manifesting in many forms.

children.text: Omityevaṃ dhyāyathātmānaṃ svasti vaḥ pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt /
children.translated_text: Meditate thus upon the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) with the syllable <s>Om</s>. May you fare well in crossing beyond darkness!

children.text: divye brahmapure vyomni ātmā sampratiṣṭhitaḥ // Dg_6.9 = DbhP_7,36.9 //
children.translated_text: In the divine city of <s>Brahman</s>, in the ether, the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is firmly established.
Consisting of mind, leader of the body of <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), established in food, having placed the heart nearby —

children.text: tadvijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrā ānandarūpam amṛtaṃ yadvibhāti // Dg_6.10 = DbhP_7,36.10 //
children.translated_text: by that realization, the wise perceive that which shines forth as the form of bliss and immortality.
The knot of the heart is severed, all doubts are cut asunder,

children.text: kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare // Dg_6.11 = DbhP_7,36.11 //
children.translated_text: and all one's <s>karmas</s> (actions) are exhausted — when that supreme, transcendent One is seen.

children.text: hiraṇmaye pare kośe virājaṃ brahma niṣkalam /
children.translated_text: In the supreme golden sheath, <s>Brahman</s> dwells — radiant, without parts.

children.text: tacchubhraṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotis tadyadātmavido viduḥ // Dg_6.12 = DbhP_7,36.12 //
children.translated_text: That is pure, the light of lights — that is what the knowers of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) know.

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ /
children.translated_text: The sun does not shine there, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine — how then could this fire?

children.text: tameva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti // Dg_6.13 = DbhP_7,36.13 //
children.translated_text: Everything shines only after That shining one; by its radiance, all this is illuminated.
<s>Brahman</s> alone is this immortal — <s>Brahman</s> in front, <s>Brahman</s> behind, <s>Brahman</s> to the south and to the north,

children.text: adhaścordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvaṃ variṣṭham // Dg_6.14 = DbhP_7,36.14 //
children.translated_text: extending below and above — <s>Brahman</s> alone is all this, the most excellent universe.
One whose experience is of this nature, that best of men is fulfilled.

children.text: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati // Dg_6.15 = DbhP_7,36.15 //
children.translated_text: Having become <s>Brahman</s>, with a serene self, he neither grieves nor desires.
Fear arises from a second, O King; from its absence, one does not fear.

children.text: na tadviyogo me 'pyasti madviyogo 'pi tasya na // Dg_6.16 = DbhP_7,36.16 //
children.translated_text: There is no separation from Me for that one, nor is there separation from that one for Me.

children.text: aham eva sa so 'haṃ vai niścitaṃ viddhi parvata /
children.translated_text: I am indeed that one, and that one is indeed I — know this with certainty, O <s>Himālaya</s>!

children.text: maddarśanaṃ tu tatra syādyatra jñānī sthito mama // Dg_6.17 = DbhP_7,36.17 //
children.translated_text: My presence is there wherever a knower of Mine abides.

children.text: nāhaṃ tīrthe na kailāse vaikuṇṭhe vā na karhicit /
children.translated_text: I do not dwell in sacred places, nor in <s>Kailāsa</s>, nor in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — never!
Rather, I dwell in the center of the heart-lotus of one who knows Me.
A single act of worship of one who knows Me yields the fruit of ten million acts of My worship.

children.text: kulaṃ pavitraṃ tasyāsti jananī kṛtakṛtyakā // Dg_6.19 = DbhP_7,36.19 //
children.translated_text: His lineage is purified, and his mother has fulfilled her purpose.
The earth is made auspicious and meritorious by the one in whose mind rests awareness of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: brahmajñānaṃ tu yatpṛṣṭaṃ tvayā parvata sattama // Dg_6.20 = DbhP_7,36.20 //
children.translated_text: As for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> that you have asked about, O best of mountains,

children.text: kathitaṃ tanmayā sarvaṃ nāto vaktavyam asti hi /
children.translated_text: all of that has been told by Me; nothing more remains to be said.

children.text: idaṃ jyeṣṭhāya putrāya bhaktiyuktāya śīline // Dg_6.21 = DbhP_7,36.21 //
children.translated_text: This is to be imparted to the eldest son who is devoted and of good conduct,

children.text: śiṣyāya ca yathoktāya vaktavyaṃ nānyathā kvacit /
children.translated_text: and to a disciple who is properly qualified — never otherwise, under any circumstances.

children.text: yasya deve parā bhaktiryathā deve tathā gurau // Dg_6.22 = DbhP_7,36.22 //
children.translated_text: One who has supreme devotion to the Divine, and equal devotion to the <s>Guru</s> (teacher),
to that great soul, these meanings that have been spoken become illuminated.

children.text: yenopadiṣṭāvidyeyaṃ sa eva parameśvaraḥ // Dg_6.23 = DbhP_7,36.23 //
children.translated_text: The one by whom this knowledge is imparted — that one is verily the supreme Lord.
To whom one is unable to render sufficient good in return, to that one the disciple remains indebted.
The bestower of the birth of <s>Brahman</s> (spiritual rebirth) is declared to be even greater than one's parents.

children.text: pitṛjātaṃ janma naṣṭaṃ netthaṃ jātaṃ kadācana /
children.translated_text: The birth obtained from parents perishes, but the birth obtained from the <s>Guru</s> never perishes.

children.text: tasmai na druhyedityādi nigamo 'pyavadannaga // Dg_6.25 = DbhP_7,36.25 //
children.translated_text: "One should never betray that one" — thus the <s>Veda</s> itself has declared, O <s>Nāga</s> (mountain)!
Therefore, the established conclusion of the scriptures is that the <s>Guru</s> (teacher), the bestower of <s>Brahman</s>, is supreme.

children.text: śive ruṣṭe gurustrātā gurau ruṣṭe na śaṅkaraḥ // Dg_6.26 = DbhP_7,36.26 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Śiva</s> is angry, the <s>Guru</s> is the protector; but when the <s>Guru</s> is angry, <s>Śaṅkara</s> cannot protect.
Therefore, with every effort, one should please the revered <s>Guru</s>, O <s>Nāga</s> (mountain)!

children.text: kāyena manasā vācā sarvadā tatparo bhavet // Dg_6.27 = DbhP_7,36.27 //
children.translated_text: With body, mind, and speech, one should always be devoted to the <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: anyathā tu kṛtaghnaḥ syāt kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Otherwise one becomes ungrateful, and for the ungrateful there is no atonement.
By <s>Indra</s>, it was told to <s>Atharvaṇa</s> with the vow of beheading —

children.text: aśvibhyāṃ kathane tasya śiraśchinnaṃ ca vajriṇā /
children.translated_text: when it was told to the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the wielder of the thunderbolt, severed his head.

children.text: aśvīyaṃ tacchiro naṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā vaidyau surottamau // Dg_6.29 = DbhP_7,36.29 //
children.translated_text: Seeing that his head was lost due to the horse-head substitution, the two divine physicians, the <s>Aśvins</s>,
reattached the sage's own head at that time.

children.text: iti saṅkaṭasampādyā brahmavidyā nagādhipa // Dg_6.30 = DbhP_7,36.30 //
children.translated_text: Thus, knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is obtainable only through great difficulty, O lord of mountains!

children.text: lābdhā yena sa dhanyaḥ syāt kṛtakṛtyaśca bhūdhara
children.translated_text: One who has attained it is truly blessed and has fulfilled all purposes, O mountain!

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ ṣaṣṭo 'dhyāyaḥ
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the sixth chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s>.
Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter of the seventh <s>Skandha</s> (book) of the <s>Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, being the sixth chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s>.

children.text:
atha saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
saptamaḥ skandhaḥ
atha saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now begins the seventh chapter.
Seventh <s>Skandha</s> (book).
Now begins the thirty-seventh chapter.
<s>Himālaya</s> said:

children.text: svīyāṃ bhaktiṃ vadasvāmba yena jñānaṃ sukhena hi /
children.translated_text: O Mother, please speak of Your own <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion), by which knowledge easily
arises in a person of moderate ability who lacks <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion).
The <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) said:
Three paths are renowned as leading to <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation), O lord of mountains:

children.text: karmayogo jñānayogo bhaktiyogaśca sattama // Dg_7.2 = DbhP_7,37.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karma Yoga</s> (the path of action), <s>Jñāna Yoga</s> (the path of knowledge), and <s>Bhakti Yoga</s> (the path of devotion), O best one!
Of the three, <s>Bhakti Yoga</s> is suitable for all and can be practiced in every way,
because of its accessibility, its being of the nature of mind, and because it causes no affliction to body, mind, or the like.
That <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) is considered to be of three kinds, according to the difference of <s>Guṇas</s> (qualities) in human beings.

children.text: parapīḍāṃ samuddiśya dambhaṃ kṛtvā puraḥsaram // Dg_7.4 = DbhP_7,37.4 //
children.translated_text: One who engages in devotion with the aim of harming others, with hypocrisy as the foremost motive,
filled with envy and anger — his devotion is <s>Tāmasī</s> (of the nature of darkness).

children.text: parapīḍādirahitaḥ svakalyāṇārtham eva ca // Dg_7.5 = DbhP_7,37.5 //
children.translated_text: One who is free from harming others and the like, but performs devotion for his own welfare alone,
always filled with desires in his heart, seeking fame, greedy for pleasures,
and who worships Me with great devotion for the attainment of those various fruits —

children.text: bhedabuddhyā tu māṃ svasmādanyāṃ jānāti pāmaraḥ /
children.translated_text: such a fool knows Me as different from himself, through the intellect of duality.

children.text: tasya bhaktiḥ samākhyātā nagādhipa tu rājasī // Dg_7.7 = DbhP_7,37.7 //
children.translated_text: His devotion is declared to be <s>Rājasī</s> (of the nature of passion), O lord of mountains!
One who offers all actions to the supreme Lord, for the cleansing of sins,

children.text: vedoktatvādavaśyaṃ tatkartavyaṃ tu mayāniśam // Dg_7.8 = DbhP_7,37.8 //
children.translated_text: thinking: "Because it is prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s>, this must certainly be done by me always" —
one of such firm conviction, who still relies on the intellect of duality,

children.text: karoti prītaye karma bhaktiḥ sā naga sattvikī // Dg_7.9 = DbhP_7,37.9 //
children.translated_text: and performs actions for the sake of pleasing the Lord — that devotion, O mountain, is <s>Sāttvikī</s> (of the nature of goodness).
This <s>Sāttvikī Bhakti</s> leads to <s>Parā Bhakti</s> (supreme devotion), since it still depends on the intellect of duality.

children.text: pūrvaprokte hyubhe bhaktī na paraprāpike mate // Dg_7.10 = DbhP_7,37.10 //
children.translated_text: The two previously mentioned forms of devotion (<s>Tāmasī</s> and <s>Rājasī</s>) are not considered to lead to <s>Parā Bhakti</s>.

children.text: adhunā parabhaktiṃ tu procyamānāṃ nibodha me /
children.translated_text: Now hear from Me about <s>Parā Bhakti</s> (supreme devotion) as I describe it.

children.text: madguṇaśravaṇaṃ nityaṃ mama nāmānukīrtanam // Dg_7.11 = DbhP_7,37.11 //
children.translated_text: Constant listening to My qualities, continuous chanting of My names,
the steady abiding of the mind in Me, who am the treasure-house of auspicious qualities and gems,

children.text: cetaso vartanaṃ caiva tailadhārāsamaṃ sadā // Dg_7.12 = DbhP_7,37.12 //
children.translated_text: always, like an unbroken stream of oil —

children.text: hetustu tatra ko vāpi na kadācidbhavedapi /
children.translated_text: and in that state, there may never be any ulterior motive whatsoever;
nor is there any desire for <s>Sāmīpya</s> (proximity), <s>Sārṣṭi</s> (equal glory), <s>Sāyujya</s> (union), or <s>Sālokya</s> (dwelling in the same realm).
One who never knows anything greater than service to Me,

children.text: sevyasevakatābhāvāt tatra mokṣaṃ na vāñchati // Dg_7.14 = DbhP_7,37.14 //
children.translated_text: and who, because of the relationship of the served and the servant, does not even desire <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation);
one who, with supreme love, meditates on Me alone, unwearied,

children.text: svābhedenaiva māṃ nityaṃ jānāti na vibhedataḥ // Dg_7.15 = DbhP_7,37.15 //
children.translated_text: who always knows Me as non-different from the Self, and not as separate;

children.text: madrūpatvena jīvānāṃ cintanaṃ kurute tu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: one who contemplates all living beings as being of My very form,

children.text: yathā svasyātmani prītistathaiva ca parātmani // Dg_7.16 = DbhP_7,37.16 //
children.translated_text: and who has the same love for the Self in others as for one's own Self;

children.text: caitanyasya samānatvānna bhedaṃ kurute tu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: one who, due to the equality of consciousness everywhere, makes no distinction,

children.text: sarvatra vartamānānāṃ sarvarūpāṃ ca sarvadā // Dg_7.17 = DbhP_7,37.17 //
children.translated_text: and who recognizes the all-pervading, all-formed presence at all times;
one who bows down to and worships all beings, even unto the lowest-born, as the Lord —

children.text: na kutrāpi drohabuddhiṃ kurute bhedavarjanāt // Dg_7.18 = DbhP_7,37.18 //
children.translated_text: and who never harbors a hostile thought toward anyone, having abandoned all sense of difference;
one who has faith in visiting places sacred to Me, and likewise in seeing My devotees,

children.text: macchāstraśravaṇe śraddhā mantratantrādiṣu prabho // Dg_7.19 = DbhP_7,37.19 //
children.translated_text: and who has faith in hearing My scriptures, <s>Mantras</s>, <s>Tantras</s>, and the like, O Lord;
one whose mind is overwhelmed with love for Me, whose body is always covered with horripilation,
whose eyes are filled with tears of love, and whose voice is choked with emotion;
one who worships Me with single-minded devotion, O lord of mountains —
Me, the <s>Īśvarī</s> (sovereign Goddess), the source of the universe, the cause of all causes;
one who always performs My sacred <s>Vratas</s> (vows), both regular and occasional,

children.text: nityaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ // Dg_7.22 = DbhP_7,37.22 //
children.translated_text: with devotion, free from miserliness and deception regarding wealth;
one who naturally has the desire to witness My festivals and also to celebrate them —

children.text: jāyate yasya niyataṃ svabhāvadeva bhūdhara // Dg_7.23 = DbhP_7,37.23 //
children.translated_text: in whom this arises spontaneously, by one's very nature, O mountain;
one who sings My names aloud and indeed dances,
free from egoism and from identification with the body;

children.text: prārabdhena yathā yacca kriyate tattathā bahvet /
children.translated_text: whatever happens according to one's <s>Prārabdha</s> (destiny from past actions), let it be so;

children.text: na me cintāsti tatrāpi dehasaṃrakṣaṇādiṣu // Dg_7.25 = DbhP_7,37.25 //
children.translated_text: one who has no concern even for the preservation of the body and the like —

children.text: iti bhaktistu yā proktā parabhaktistu sā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: such devotion as has been described is known as <s>Parā Bhakti</s> (supreme devotion),

children.text: yasyāṃ devyatiriktaṃ tu na kiñcidapi bhāvyate // Dg_7.26 = DbhP_7,37.26 //
children.translated_text: in which nothing whatsoever apart from the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) is contemplated.

children.text: itthaṃ jātā parā bhaktiryasya bhūdhara tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: One in whom such <s>Parā Bhakti</s> (supreme devotion) has truly arisen, O mountain,

children.text: tadaiva tasya cinmātre madrūpe vilayo bhavet // Dg_7.27 = DbhP_7,37.27 //
children.translated_text: at that very moment, dissolution into My form, which is pure consciousness, takes place.

children.text: bhaktestu yā parā kāṣṭhā saiva jñānaṃ prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: The highest culmination of <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) is itself proclaimed as <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: vairāgyasya ca sīmā sā jñāne tadubhayaṃ yataḥ // Dg_7.28 = DbhP_7,37.28 //
children.translated_text: and that is also the limit of <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion), for both are contained in <s>Jñāna</s>.
If, even after devotion has been practiced, due to the force of <s>Prārabdha</s> (destiny), O mountain,

children.text: na jāyate mama jñānaṃ maṇidvīpaṃ sa gacchati // Dg_7.29 = DbhP_7,37.29 //
children.translated_text: knowledge of Me does not arise, that person goes to <s>Maṇidvīpa</s> (the Jewel Island, the Devī's abode).
Having gone there, one enjoys all pleasures even without desiring them,

children.text: tadante mama cidrūpajñānaṃ samyagbhavennaga // Dg_7.30 = DbhP_7,37.30 //
children.translated_text: and at the end of that period, complete knowledge of My true nature as pure consciousness arises, O mountain.
By that knowledge one is forever liberated — liberation comes through knowledge alone and not otherwise.

children.text: ihaiva yasya jñānaṃ syāddhṛdgatapratyagātmanaḥ // Dg_7.31 = DbhP_7,37.31 //
children.translated_text: For one in whom knowledge of the inner Self dwelling in the heart arises even here in this life,
whose innermost awareness rests in My supreme consciousness — that one's vital breaths do not depart.

children.text: brahmaiva saṃstadāpnoti brahmaiva brahma veda yaḥ // Dg_7.32 = DbhP_7,37.32 //
children.translated_text: That one, being <s>Brahman</s>, attains <s>Brahman</s> — <s>Brahman</s> alone is known by one who knows <s>Brahman</s>.
Like gold around the neck — it is hidden only due to ignorance;

children.text: jñānādajñānanāśena labdhameva hi labhyate // Dg_7.33 = DbhP_7,37.33 //
children.translated_text: through knowledge, by the destruction of ignorance, what was already attained is indeed realized.
My form is other than the known and other than the unknown, O best of mountains!

children.text: yathādarśe tathātmani yathā jale tathā pitṛloke // Dg_7.34 = DbhP_7,37.34 //
children.translated_text: As in a mirror, so in the Self; as in water, so in the world of the ancestors;

children.text: chāyātapau yathā svacchau viviktau tadvadeva hi /
children.translated_text: as shade and light are clearly distinct — just so indeed,

children.text: mama loke bhavejjñānaṃ dvaitabhāvavivarjitam // Dg_7.35 = DbhP_7,37.35 //
children.translated_text: in My realm, knowledge arises free from all duality.
But if one who possesses <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion) alone, devoid of <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), were to die,

children.text: brahmaloke vasennityaṃ yāvatkalpaṃ tataḥ param // Dg_7.36 = DbhP_7,37.36 //
children.translated_text: that one dwells in <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of Brahmā) perpetually for the duration of a <s>Kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle); then, after that,

children.text: śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe bhavettasya janiḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: that one takes birth again in the home of the pure and prosperous.

children.text: karoti sādhanaṃ paścāttato jñānaṃ hi jāyate // Dg_7.37 = DbhP_7,37.37 //
children.translated_text: Then, performing <s>Sādhana</s> (spiritual practice) again, knowledge indeed arises.
Through many births, O King, knowledge is attained — not in a single birth.

children.text: tataḥ sarvaprayatnena jñānārthaṃ yatnamāśrayet // Dg_7.38 = DbhP_7,37.38 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, with every possible effort, one should strive for the attainment of knowledge.
Otherwise, great destruction ensues, for this human birth is rare to obtain again.

children.text: tatrāpi prathame varṇe vedaprāptiśca durlabhā // Dg_7.39 = DbhP_7,37.39 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, even within that, being born in the first <s>Varṇa</s> (class) and attaining the <s>Vedas</s> is rare.
The sixfold wealth beginning with <s>Śama</s> (tranquility), and likewise the perfection of <s>Yoga</s>,
and the attainment of an excellent <s>Guru</s> (teacher) — all of this is indeed rare.
Likewise, the sharpness of the senses and the refinement of the body —

children.text: anekajanmapuṇyaistu mokṣecchā jāyate tataḥ // Dg_7.41 = DbhP_7,37.41 //
children.translated_text: only through the merit of many births does the desire for <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) arise.
Even when all these favorable conditions arise, a person

children.text: jñānārthaṃ naiva yatate tasya janma nirarthakam // Dg_7.42 = DbhP_7,37.42 //
children.translated_text: who does not strive for knowledge — his birth is in vain.
Therefore, O King, according to one's capacity, one should strive for the attainment of knowledge.
At every step, one certainly obtains the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).

children.text: ghṛtamiva payasi nigūḍhaṃ bhūte bhūte ca vasati vijñānam /
children.translated_text: Just as butter lies hidden in milk, so <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) dwells in every being.

children.text: satataṃ manthayitavyaṃ manasā manthānabhūtena // Dg_7.44 = DbhP_7,37.44 //
children.translated_text: It must be constantly churned with the mind as the churning rod.
Having obtained <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), one becomes fulfilled — this is the proclamation of <s>Vedānta</s>.

children.text: sarvamuktaṃ samāsena kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi // Dg_7.45 = DbhP_7,37.45 //
children.translated_text: Everything has been told in brief; what more do you wish to hear?

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s> — thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter of the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, within the <s>Devīgītā</s>.
Eighth chapter, seventh book; now the thirty-eighth chapter.
<s>Himālaya</s> said:
How many places on the earth are to be visited, O Goddess of gods, that are foremost, sacred, and most dear to the <s>Devī</s>?

children.text: mukhyāni ca pavitrāṇi devīpriyatamāni ca // Dg_8.1 = DbhP_7,38.1 //
children.translated_text: And also which <s>vratas</s> (observances) bestow satisfaction, and which festivals too?
Tell me all that, O Mother of the gods, by which a person becomes fulfilled.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ deva me mātaḥ kṛtakṛtyo yato naraḥ // Dg_8.2 = DbhP_7,38.2 //
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:
Everything visible is my abode; all times are imbued with <s>vrata</s> (observance);

children.text: sarvaṃ dṛśyaṃ mama sthānaṃ sarve kālā vratātmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: festivals exist at all times, since I am the one whose form is everything.

children.text: utsavāḥ sarvakāleṣu yato 'haṃ sarvarūpiṇī // Dg_8.3 = DbhP_7,38.3 //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, out of affection for devotees, a little shall now be told.
Listen attentively, O king of mountains, to my words.

children.text: śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā nagarāja vaco mama // Dg_8.4 = DbhP_7,38.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kolāpura</s> is a great sacred site where <s>Lakṣmī</s> ever abides;

children.text: kolāpuraṃ mahāsthānaṃ yatra lakṣmīḥ sadā sthitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Mātṛpura</s> is the second, presided over by <s>Reṇukā</s>, a supreme site.

children.text: mātuḥ puraṃ dvitīyaṃ ca reṇukādhiṣṭhitaṃ param // Dg_8.5 = DbhP_7,38.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tulajāpura</s> is the third, and likewise <s>Saptaśṛṅga</s>;
the great site of <s>Hiṅgulā</s>, and likewise that of <s>Jvālāmukhī</s>.

children.text: hiṅgulāyā mahāsthānaṃ jvālāmukhyāstathaiva ca // Dg_8.6 = DbhP_7,38.6 //
children.translated_text: The supreme site of <s>Śākambharī</s>, the excellent site of <s>Bhrāmarī</s>,
the site of the glorious <s>Raktadantikā</s>, and likewise the site of <s>Durgā</s>.

children.text: śrīraktadantikāsthānaṃ durgāsthānaṃ tathaiva ca // Dg_8.7 = DbhP_7,38.7 //
children.translated_text: The site of <s>Vindhyācalanivāsinī</s> (the one who dwells on the Vindhya mountain) is the most supreme of all;
the great site of <s>Annapūrṇā</s>, and <s>Kāñcīpura</s>, unsurpassed.
The supreme site of <s>Bhīmādevī</s>, and also the site of <s>Vimalā</s>,
the great site of the glorious <s>Candralā</s>, and also the site of <s>Kauśikī</s>.
The supreme site of <s>Nīlāmbā</s> is on the peak of <s>Nīlaparvata</s> (Blue Mountain);
the site of <s>Jāmbūnadeśvarī</s>, and likewise the auspicious <s>Śrīnagara</s>.

children.text: jāmbūnadeśvarīsthānaṃ tathā śrīnagaraṃ śubham // Dg_8.10 = DbhP_7,38.10 //
children.translated_text: The great site of <s>Guhyakālī</s>, which is established in <s>Nepāla</s>;
the supreme site of <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, and that which is celebrated in <s>Cidambara</s>.

children.text: mīnākṣyāḥ paraṃ sthānaṃ yacca proktaṃ cidambare // Dg_8.11 = DbhP_7,38.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vedāraṇya</s> is a great site presided over by <s>Sundarī</s>;
<s>Ekāmbara</s> is a great site established by the supreme <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: ekāmbaraṃ mahāsthānaṃ paraśaktyā pratiṣṭhitam // Dg_8.12 = DbhP_7,38.12 //
children.translated_text: The supreme site of <s>Mahālasā</s>, and likewise of <s>Yogeśvarī</s>;
and also the site of <s>Nīlasarasvatī</s>, renowned in the land of <s>Cīna</s> (China).

children.text: tathā nīlasarasvatyāḥ sthānaṃ cīneṣu viśrutam // Dg_8.13 = DbhP_7,38.13 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Vaidyanātha</s>, the site of <s>Bagalā</s> is considered the most supreme;
the glorious <s>Maṇidvīpa</s> (Jewel Island) is remembered as my own, belonging to the glorious <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s>.

children.text: śrīmacchrībhuvaneśvaryā maṇidvīpaṃ mama smṛtam // Dg_8.14 = DbhP_7,38.14 //
children.translated_text: The <s>yonimaṇḍala</s> (sacred circle of the womb) of the glorious <s>Tripurabhairavī</s> at <s>Kāmākhyā</s>,
is the jewel among sacred sites on the earth, inhabited by <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (the Great Illusion).
There is no site superior to this anywhere on the surface of the earth,
where the <s>Devī</s> herself becomes <s>rajasvalā</s> (menstruating) every month.

children.text: pratimāsaṃ bhaveddevī yatra sākṣādrajasvalā // Dg_8.16 = DbhP_7,38.16 //
children.translated_text: All the deities there have assumed the form of mountains;
even the great deities dwell upon the mountains.

children.text: parvateṣu vasantyeva mahatyo devatā api // Dg_8.17 = DbhP_7,38.17 //
children.translated_text: The entire earth there is regarded by the wise as having the form of the <s>Devī</s>;

children.text: tatratyā pṛthivī sarvā devīrūpā smṛtā budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: there is no site superior to the <s>yonimaṇḍala</s> (sacred circle) of <s>Kāmākhyā</s>.

children.text: nātaḥ parataraṃ sthānaṃ kāmākhyāyonimaṇḍalāt // Dg_8.18 = DbhP_7,38.18 //
children.translated_text: The supreme site of <s>Gāyatrī</s> is declared to be the glorious <s>Puṣkara</s>;
at <s>Amareśa</s> she is <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, at <s>Prabhāsa</s> she is <s>Puṣkarekṣiṇī</s> (the lotus-eyed one).

children.text: amareśe caṇḍikā syātprabhāse puṣkarekṣiṇī // Dg_8.19 = DbhP_7,38.19 //
children.translated_text: At the great site of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, the <s>Devī</s> is <s>Liṅgadhāriṇī</s> (bearer of the liṅga);

children.text: naimiṣe tu mahāsthāne devī sā liṅgadhāriṇī /
children.translated_text: at <s>Puṣkarākṣa</s> she is <s>Puruhūtā</s>, and at <s>Āṣāḍha</s> she is <s>Rati</s>.

children.text: puruhūtā puṣkarākṣe aṣāḍhai ca ratistathā // Dg_8.20 = DbhP_7,38.20 //
children.translated_text: At the great site of <s>Caṇḍamuṇḍī</s>, the supreme goddess is <s>Daṇḍinī</s> (the staff-bearer);
at <s>Bhārabhūti</s> she is <s>Bhūti</s> (prosperity), at <s>Nākula</s> she is <s>Nakuleśvarī</s>.
At <s>Hariścandra</s> she is <s>Candrikā</s> (moonlight), at <s>Śrīgiri</s> she is known as <s>Śāṅkarī</s>;

children.text: candrikā tu hariścandre śrīgirau śāṅkarī smṛtā /
children.translated_text: at <s>Japyeśvara</s> she is <s>Triśūlā</s> (the trident-bearing one), and at <s>Āmrātakeśvara</s> she is <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (the subtle one).

children.text: japyeśvare triśūlā syātsūkṣmā cāmrātakeśvare // Dg_8.22 = DbhP_7,38.22 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Mahākāla</s> she is <s>Śāṅkarī</s>, at the one called <s>Madhyama</s> she is <s>Śarvāṇī</s>;
at the great sacred site called <s>Kedāra</s>, the <s>Devī</s> is <s>Mārgadāyinī</s> (the one who shows the path).

children.text: kedārākhye mahākṣetre devī sā mārgadāyinī // Dg_8.23 = DbhP_7,38.23 //
children.translated_text: At the place called <s>Bhairava</s> she is <s>Bhairavī</s>, at <s>Gayā</s> she is known as <s>Maṅgalā</s> (the auspicious one);

children.text: bhairavākhye bhairavī sā gayāyāṃ maṅgalā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: at <s>Kurukṣetra</s> she is <s>Sthāṇupriyā</s> (beloved of Śiva), and at <s>Nākula</s> she is <s>Svāyambhuvī</s> (the self-manifested).

children.text: sthāṇupriyā kurukṣetre svāyambhuvyapi nākule // Dg_8.24 = DbhP_7,38.24 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Kanakhala</s> she is <s>Ugrā</s> (the fierce one), at <s>Vimaleśvara</s> she is <s>Viśveśā</s> (mistress of all);
at <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s> she is <s>Mahānandā</s> (great bliss), at <s>Mahendra</s> she is <s>Mahāntakā</s> (the great destroyer).

children.text: aṭṭahāse mahānandā mahendre tu mahāntakā // Dg_8.25 = DbhP_7,38.25 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Bhīma</s> she is called <s>Bhīmeśvarī</s>, and at the site of <s>Vastrāpatha</s>,

children.text: bhīme bhīmeśvarī proktā sthāne vastrāpathe punaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhavānī</s> is called <s>Śāṅkarī</s>, and at <s>Ardhakoṭika</s> she is <s>Rudrāṇī</s>.

children.text: bhavānī śāṅkarī proktā rudrāṇī tvardhakoṭike // Dg_8.26 = DbhP_7,38.26 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Avimukta</s> she is <s>Viśālākṣī</s> (the large-eyed one), at <s>Mahālaya</s> she is <s>Mahābhāgā</s> (the greatly fortunate);
at <s>Gokarṇa</s> she is <s>Bhadrakarṇī</s>, at <s>Bhadrakarṇaka</s> she is <s>Bhadrā</s> (the auspicious one).

children.text: gokarṇe bhadrakarṇī syādbhadrā syādbhadrakarṇake // Dg_8.27 = DbhP_7,38.27 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Suvarṇākṣa</s> she is <s>Utpalākṣī</s> (the lotus-eyed one), at the place called <s>Sthāṇu</s> she is <s>Sthāṇvīśā</s>;
at <s>Kamalālaya</s> she is <s>Kamalā</s> (the lotus one), at <s>Chagalaṇḍaka</s> she is <s>Pracaṇḍā</s> (the fierce one).

children.text: kamalālaye tu kamalā pracaṇḍā chagalaṇḍake // Dg_8.28 = DbhP_7,38.28 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Kuraṇḍala</s> she is <s>Trisandhyā</s> (of the three junctions), at <s>Mākoṭa</s> she is <s>Mukuṭeśvarī</s> (the crowned goddess);
at <s>Maṇḍaleśa</s> she is <s>Śāṇḍakī</s>, and at <s>Kālañjara</s> she is <s>Kālī</s>.

children.text: maṇḍaleśe śāṇḍakī syātkālī kālañjare punaḥ // Dg_8.29 = DbhP_7,38.29 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> she is called <s>Dhvani</s> (sound), at <s>Sthūlakeśvara</s> she is <s>Sthūlā</s> (the massive one);
in the lotus of the heart of the wise, she is <s>Hṛllekhā</s>, the supreme goddess.

children.text: jñānināṃ hṛdayāmbhoje hṛllekhā parameśvarī // Dg_8.30 = DbhP_7,38.30 //
children.translated_text: These sites most dear to the <s>Devī</s> have been declared;
having first heard the greatness of each respective sacred site, O best of mountains,

children.text: tattatkṣetrasya māhātmyaṃ śrutvā pūrvaṃ nagottama // Dg_8.31 = DbhP_7,38.31 //
children.translated_text: one should then worship the <s>Devī</s> according to the prescribed method.
Alternatively, all sacred sites exist in <s>Kāśī</s>, O best of mountains.

children.text: athavā sarvakṣetrāṇi kāśyāṃ santi nagottama // Dg_8.32 = DbhP_7,38.32 //
children.translated_text: One who is devoted to the worship of the <s>Devī</s> should always dwell there,
beholding those sacred places and ceaselessly chanting the <s>Devī</s>'s name,

children.text: tāni sthānāni sampaśyañjapandevīṃ nirantaram // Dg_8.33 = DbhP_7,38.33 //
children.translated_text: meditating on her lotus feet, one becomes liberated from bondage.
One who recites these names of the <s>Devī</s> upon rising in the morning —

children.text: imāni devīnāmāni prātarutthāya yaḥ paṭhet // Dg_8.34 = DbhP_7,38.34 //
children.translated_text: his sins are instantly reduced to ashes, O mountain, without delay.
One who recites these pure names before the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> during <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) —
all his ancestors become liberated and attain the supreme destination.
Now I shall tell you about the <s>vratas</s> (sacred vows), O you of excellent vows,

children.text: adhunā kathayiṣyāmi vratāni tava suvrata // Dg_8.36 = DbhP_7,38.36 //
children.translated_text: which are to be performed diligently by both women and men.
The <s>vrata</s> called <s>Anantatṛtīyā</s>, the <s>Rasakalyāṇinī vrata</s>,
the one called <s>Ārdrānandakara</s> (joy-giving on the Ārdrā day), and also the <s>vrata</s> of the third <s>tithi</s>,

children.text: ārdrānandakaraṃ nāmnā tṛtīyāyā vratam ca yat /
children.translated_text: the <s>Śukravāra vrata</s> (Friday observance), and likewise the <s>Kṛṣṇa Caturdaśī</s> (fourteenth day of the dark fortnight),

children.text: śukravāravrataṃ caiva tathā kṛṣṇacaturdaśī // Dg_8.38 = DbhP_7,38.38 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhaumavāra vrata</s> (Tuesday observance), and also the <s>Pradoṣa vrata</s>,
in which the great god <s>Mahādeva</s>, having seated the <s>Devī</s> upon a throne,

children.text: yatra devo mahādevo devīṃ saṃsthāpya viṣṭare // Dg_8.39 = DbhP_7,38.39 //
children.translated_text: dances before her together with the gods at the onset of night.
Having fasted at the beginning of the night, one should worship <s>Śivā</s> (the auspicious goddess) at <s>pradoṣa</s> (twilight);

children.text: tatropoṣya rajanyādau pradoṣe pūjayecchivām // Dg_8.40 = DbhP_7,38.40 //
children.translated_text: this should be done especially every fortnight, as it brings pleasure to the <s>Devī</s>.
The <s>Somavāra vrata</s> (Monday observance) is also exceedingly dear to me, O mountain.
In that too, having worshipped the <s>Devī</s>, one should take food at night.
The two <s>Navarātra</s> observances are also a pleasing <s>vrata</s>.

children.text: navarātradvayaṃ caiva vrataṃ prītikaraṃ // Dg_8.42 = DbhP_7,38.42 //
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever performs these and other regular and occasional
<s>vratas</s> for my satisfaction, free from envy,

children.text: vratāni kurute yo vai matprītyarthaṃ vimatsaraḥ // Dg_8.43 = DbhP_7,38.43 //
children.translated_text: attains union with me — he is my devotee, he is dear to me.

children.text: prāpnoti mama sāyujyaṃ sa me bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should also perform festivals, O lord — the joyous swing festival (<s>Dolotsava</s>),
the sleeping festival (<s>Śayanotsava</s>), and likewise the waking festival (<s>Jāgaraṇotsava</s>),
the chariot festival (<s>Rathotsava</s>) for me, and also the <s>Damanotsava</s> (festival of the Damana plant).

children.text: rathotsavaṃ ca me kuryāddamanotsavameva ca // Dg_8.45 = DbhP_7,38.45 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pavitrotsava</s> (purification festival) in the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> is also pleasing;
my devotee should always perform such great festivals.

children.text: mama bhaktaḥ sadā kuryādevamanyānmahotsavān // Dg_8.46 = DbhP_7,38.46 //
children.translated_text: One should lovingly feed my devotees, as well as married women (<s>suvāsinīs</s>),
and also maidens and young boys, with the understanding that they are me, with one's mind absorbed in me.
Free from miserliness regarding wealth, one should worship them with flowers and other offerings.
Whoever does this with devotion every year, unwearied,

children.text: ya evaṃ kurute bhaktyā prativarṣamatandritaḥ // Dg_8.48 = DbhP_7,38.48 //
children.translated_text: he is blessed, he is fulfilled, and he is readily a vessel for my love.
Everything that brings me pleasure has been told in brief;

children.text: sarvamuktaṃ samāsena mama prītipradāyakam // Dg_8.49 = DbhP_7,38.49 //
children.translated_text: it should not be given to one who is not a disciple, nor ever to one who lacks devotion.

children.text: nāśiṣyāya pradātavyaṃ nābaktāya kadācana // Dg_8.50 = DbhP_7,38.50 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s> — thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter of the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, within the <s>Devīgītā</s>.

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāmaṣṭamo 'dhyāya -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāmaṣṭatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Ninth chapter, seventh book; now the thirty-ninth chapter.
<s>Himālaya</s> said:
O Goddess of gods, great sovereign, ocean of compassion, O <s>Ambikā</s>,
tell me now properly the correct procedure of worship of yourself.

children.text: brūhi pūjāvidhiṃ samyagyathāvadadhunā nijam // Dg_9.1 = DbhP_7,39.1 //
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:
I shall describe the procedure of worship of <s>Ambikā</s>, O king, as is dear to her;
listen with utmost faith, O foremost among mountains.

children.text: atyantaśraddhayā sārdhaṃ śṛṇu parvatapuṅgava // Dg_9.2 = DbhP_7,39.2 //
children.translated_text: My worship is of two kinds: external and internal.

children.text: dvividhā mama pūjā syād vāhyā cābhyantarāpi ca /
children.translated_text: The external too is declared to be of two kinds: <s>Vaidikī</s> (Vedic) and <s>Tāntrikī</s> (Tantric).

children.text: bāhyāpi dvividhā proktā vaidikī tāntrikī tathā // Dg_9.3 = DbhP_7,39.3 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaidikī</s> is also of two kinds according to the distinction of <s>mūrti</s> (form), O mountain;
the <s>Vaidikī</s> is to be performed by those who follow the Vedas, who are endowed with Vedic initiation.

children.text: vaidikī vaidikaiḥ kāryā vedadīkṣāsamanvitaiḥ // Dg_9.4 = DbhP_7,39.4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Tāntrikī</s> is undertaken by those who possess initiation as prescribed in the <s>Tantras</s>;
thus, a foolish person who acts in a contrary manner without knowing this secret of worship

children.text: itthaṃ pūjārahasyaṃ ca na jñātvā viparītakam // Dg_9.5 = DbhP_7,39.5 //
children.translated_text: surely falls in every way.

children.text: karoti yo naro mūḍhaḥ sa patatyeva sarvathā /
children.translated_text: Of these, I shall first describe the <s>Vaidikī</s> (Vedic) method.

children.text: tatra yā vaidikī proktā prathamā tāṃ vadāmyaham // Dg_9.6 = DbhP_7,39.6 //
children.translated_text: That which is my direct supreme form, which you have beheld, O mountain —
having infinite heads, eyes, and infinite feet, the great one,
endowed with all powers, the supreme mover beyond the highest —
that alone one should worship daily, bow to, meditate upon, and remember.
Thus the nature of the first mode of worship has been described, O mountain.
Being peaceful, with a concentrated mind, free from hypocrisy and pride,
be devoted to That, sacrifice to That, take refuge in That alone.

children.text: tatparo bhava tadyājī tadeva śaraṇaṃ vraja /
children.translated_text: Behold That alone with your mind, chant and meditate upon it always.

children.text: tadeva cetasā paśya japa dhyāyasva sarvadā // Dg_9.10 = DbhP_7,39.10 //
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge in my nature with undivided, love-filled <s>bhakti</s> (devotion),
satisfy me alone through <s>yajñas</s> (sacrifices), <s>tapas</s> (austerities), and <s>dāna</s> (charity).
Thus, by my grace, you shall be freed from the bondage of worldly existence.
Those who are devoted to me, whose minds are attached to me, are considered the best of devotees.

children.text: matparā ye madāsaktacittā bhaktavarā matāḥ // Dg_9.12 = DbhP_7,39.12 //
children.translated_text: I promise that I shall swiftly deliver them from this worldly existence.
Through meditation combined with action, or through <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: dhyānena karmayuktena bhaktijñānena vā punaḥ // Dg_9.13 = DbhP_7,39.13 //
children.translated_text: I am attainable in every way, O king, but not through mere ritualistic actions alone.
From <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct) arises <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), and from <s>bhakti</s> arises the Supreme.

children.text: dharmātsañjāyate bhaktirbhaktyā sañjāyate param // Dg_9.14 = DbhP_7,39.14 //
children.translated_text: That which is enjoined by <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>Smṛti</s> (remembered tradition) is proclaimed as <s>Dharma</s>;
that which is declared by other scriptures is called a mere semblance of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: anyaśāstreṇa yaḥ prokto dharmābhāsaḥ sa ucyate // Dg_9.15 = DbhP_7,39.15 //
children.translated_text: From me, the omniscient and omnipotent, the <s>Veda</s> has arisen;
since there is no ignorance in me, the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) is never without authority.

children.text: ajñānasya mamābhāvādapramāṇā na ca śrutiḥ // Dg_9.16 = DbhP_7,39.16 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Smṛtis</s> (law codes) have come forth having grasped the meaning of <s>Śruti</s>;
hence the authority of the codes of <s>Manu</s> and others, and of the <s>Śrutis</s>, is accepted.

children.text: manvādīnāṃ śrutīnāṃ ca tataḥ prāmāṇyamiṣyate // Dg_9.17 = DbhP_7,39.17 //
children.translated_text: Sometimes others have spoken with a side-glance toward Tantric meaning;
that portion of <s>dharma</s> should not be accepted by followers of the Vedas.

children.text: dharmaṃ vadanti soṃśastu naivagrāhyo 'sti vaidikaiḥ // Dg_9.18 = DbhP_7,39.18 //
children.translated_text: Because the authors of other scriptures are born of ignorance,
and because their works are tainted by the fault of ignorance, what they state has no authority.
Therefore, one who desires liberation should in every way resort to the <s>Veda</s> for <s>dharma</s>.
Just as a king's command is never violated in the world,

children.text: rājājñā ca yathā loke hanyate na kadācana // Dg_9.20 = DbhP_7,39.20 //
children.translated_text: so is the <s>Śruti</s>, the command of the sovereign of all, namely myself — how can it be abandoned by men?

children.text: sarveśānyā mamājñā sā śrutistyājyā kathaṃ nṛbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of protecting my command, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Kṣatriya</s> castes exist.
For the purpose of protecting My command, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Kṣatriya</s> castes [were created].

children.text: mayā sṛṣṭāstato jñeyaṃ rahasyaṃ me śrutervacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Created by me—therefore know the secret word of my <s>Śruti</s> (scripture):

children.text: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhūdhara // Dg_9.22 = DbhP_7,39.22 //
children.translated_text: whenever there is a decline of <s>dharma</s>, O bearer of the earth, (Dg 9.22)
and a rise of <s>adharma</s>, then I assume various forms.
The division of gods and demons also came about from this very [principle], O king. (Dg 9.23)

children.text: ye na kurvanti taddharmaṃ tacchikṣārthaṃ mayā sadā /
children.translated_text: Those who do not practice that <s>dharma</s>—for their instruction, by me always
hells have been produced, fear of which [comes] from hearing [about them]. (Dg 9.24)
One who, abandoning the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Vedas</s>, resorts to another <s>dharma</s>—
the king should banish such transgressors of <s>dharma</s> from his own land. (Dg 9.25)

children.text: brāhmaṇairna ca sambhāṣyāḥ paṅktigrāhyā na ca dvijaiḥ /
children.translated_text: They should not be spoken with by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, nor accepted in their row by the twice-born.

children.text: anyāni yāni śāstrāṇi loke 'sminvividhāni ca // Dg_9.26 = DbhP_7,39.26 //
children.translated_text: Whatever other various scriptures exist in this world (Dg 9.26)
that contradict <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> are entirely <s>tāmasic</s> (of the quality of darkness).

children.text: vāmaṃ kāpālakaṃ caiva kaulakaṃ bhairavāgamaḥ // Dg_9.27 = DbhP_7,39.27 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Vāma</s>, the <s>Kāpālaka</s>, the <s>Kaulaka</s>, and the <s>Bhairavāgama</s>— (Dg 9.27)
were composed by <s>Śiva</s> for the purpose of delusion alone, not for any other reason.

children.text: dakṣaśāpādbhṛgoḥ śāpāddadhīcasya ca śāpataḥ // Dg_9.28 = DbhP_7,39.28 //
children.translated_text: By the curse of <s>Dakṣa</s>, by the curse of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and by the curse of <s>Dadhīca</s>, (Dg 9.28)
those excellent <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who were burnt were expelled from the Vedic path.
For their gradual upliftment, as a series of steps, (Dg 9.29)
the <s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Saura</s>, <s>Śākta</s>,

children.text: gāṇapatyā āgamāśca praṇītāḥ śaṅkareṇa tu // Dg_9.30 = DbhP_7,39.30 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Gāṇapatya</s> <s>Āgamas</s> were composed by <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (Dg 9.30)
In those, some portions not contradicting the <s>Vedas</s> are also stated here and there;

children.text: vaidikaistadgrahe deṣo na bhavatyeva karhicit // Dg_9.31 = DbhP_7,39.31 //
children.translated_text: for Vedic practitioners, no fault arises from accepting those [portions]. (Dg 9.31)
But in all matters that differ from the <s>Vedas</s>, a twice-born person has no authority.
One who lacks authority in the <s>Vedas</s>, however, may have authority in those [texts]. (Dg 9.32)
Therefore, with every effort, a Vedic practitioner should resort to the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: dharmeṇa sahitaṃ jñānaṃ paraṃ brahma prakāśayet // Dg_9.33 = DbhP_7,39.33 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge combined with <s>dharma</s> reveals the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. (Dg 9.33)
Having abandoned all desires and taken refuge in me alone,
compassionate toward all beings, free from pride and egoism, (Dg 9.34)
with minds fixed on me, their life-breath devoted to me, delighting in narrating my abode,

children.text: saṃnyāsino vanasthāśca gṛhasthā brahmacāriṇaḥ // Dg_9.35 = DbhP_7,39.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>sannyāsins</s>, forest-dwellers, householders, and <s>brahmacārins</s>— (Dg 9.35)
they always worship with devotion the <s>yoga</s> known as the Lord's.
For those who are ever undivided [from me], I dispel the darkness born of ignorance (Dg 9.36)
with the light of the sun of knowledge—there is no doubt.

children.text: itthaṃ vaidikapūjāyāḥ prathamāyā nagādhipa // Dg_9.37 = DbhP_7,39.37 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O lord of mountains, the form of the first, Vedic worship (Dg 9.37)
has been briefly stated; now I shall speak of the second.

children.text: mūrtau vā sthaṇḍile vāpi tathā sūryendumaṇḍale // Dg_9.38 = DbhP_7,39.38 //
children.translated_text: In an image, or on a consecrated ground, or in the disc of the sun or moon, (Dg 9.38)
or in water, or in a <s>bāṇaliṅga</s>, or in a <s>yantra</s>, or on a great canvas—

children.text: tathā śrīhṛdayāmbhoje dhyātvā devīṃ parātparām // Dg_9.39 = DbhP_7,39.39 //
children.translated_text: or in the lotus of one's own heart—having meditated on the <s>Devī</s>, supreme beyond the supreme, (Dg 9.39)
endowed with qualities (<s>saguṇā</s>), full of compassion, youthful, of the hue of the rising sun,
the ultimate limit of the essence of beauty, beautiful in all her limbs, (Dg 9.40)
overflowing with the rasa of love (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), ever anxious to relieve the suffering of her devotees,
the gracious Mother of benign countenance, adorned with a crescent moon as her crest, (Dg 9.41)
holding the noose, goad, and the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness, the embodiment of bliss—
one should worship her with offerings according to one's means. (Dg 9.42)
As long as one has no capacity for the inner worship,

children.text: tāvadbāhyāmimāṃ pūjāṃ śrayejjāte tu tāṃ tyajet // Dg_9.43 = DbhP_7,39.43 //
children.translated_text: one should resort to this external worship; when [the capacity] arises, one should abandon it. (Dg 9.43)

children.text: ābhyantarā tu yā pūjā sā tu saṃvillayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The inner worship is held to be the dissolution [of the mind] in pure consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>).

children.text: saṃvideva paraṃ rūpamupādhirahitaṃ mama // Dg_9.44 = DbhP_7,39.44 //
children.translated_text: Pure consciousness alone is my supreme form, free from all limiting adjuncts. (Dg 9.44)

children.text: ataḥ saṃvidi madrūpe cetaḥ sthāpyaṃ nirāśrayam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mind should be established, without support, in pure consciousness, which is my form.

children.text: saṃvidrūpātiriktaṃ tu mithyā māyāmayaṃ jagat // Dg_9.45 = DbhP_7,39.45 //
children.translated_text: Whatever exceeds the form of pure consciousness is false, illusory, and the world of <s>Māyā</s>. (Dg 9.45)
Therefore, for the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s>, [one should meditate on] the Witness, of the nature of the Self,
with a mind free from mentation, united in <s>yoga</s>. (Dg 9.46)
Hereafter, the elaboration of external worship is spoken by me.

children.text: sāvadhānena manasā śṛṇu parvatasattama // Dg_9.47 = DbhP_7,39.47 //
children.translated_text: Listen with attentive mind, O best of mountains. (Dg 9.47)

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ navamo 'dhyāyaḥ -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāmekonacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s>—thus the thirty-ninth chapter of the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devī Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.
The tenth chapter—the seventh book, now the fortieth chapter.
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:
Having risen in the morning, one should contemplate on one's head a radiant lotus,

children.text: karpūrābhaṃ smarettatra śrīguruṃ nijarūpiṇam // Dg_10.1 = DbhP_7,40.1 //
children.translated_text: and there remember the <s>Śrīguru</s>, luminous as camphor, of one's own form. (Dg 10.1)
Well-pleased, adorned with shining ornaments, accompanied by his <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: namaskṛtya tato devīṃ kuṇḍalīṃ saṃsmaredbudhaḥ // Dg_10.2 = DbhP_7,40.2 //
children.translated_text: having bowed, the wise one should then remember the <s>Devī</s> <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>: (Dg 10.2)
She who shines in the first journey [upward], who becomes immortal nectar in the return,
who moves within the inner path—I take refuge in that woman of blissful form. (Dg 10.3)
Having thus meditated on her in the center of the crown-flame, of the form of <s>Saccidānanda</s>,

children.text: māṃ dhyāyedatha śaucāditriyāḥ sarvāḥ samāpayet // Dg_10.4 = DbhP_7,40.4 //
children.translated_text: one should meditate on me, and then complete all rites beginning with purification. (Dg 10.4)
Then, having offered the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation) for my pleasure, the best of twice-born

children.text: homānte svāsane sthitvā pūjāsaṅkalpamācaret // Dg_10.5 = DbhP_7,40.5 //
children.translated_text: should, after the oblation, sit on his own seat and perform the resolve of worship (<s>pūjāsaṅkalpa</s>). (Dg 10.5)
Having first performed purification of the elements (<s>bhūtaśuddhi</s>) and the placing of the seed-syllables (<s>mātṛkānyāsa</s>),
one should always perform the placing of the <s>Hrīṃ</s>-syllable seed-letters. (Dg 10.6)

children.text: mūlādhāre hakāraṃ ca hṛdaye ca rakārakam /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'ha' at the <s>Mūlādhāra</s>, and 'ra' at the heart,

children.text: bhrūmadhye tadvadīkāraṃ hrīṅkāraṃ mastake nyaset // Dg_10.7 = DbhP_7,40.7 //
children.translated_text: likewise 'ī' between the eyebrows, and <s>Hrīṃ</s> should be placed at the crown. (Dg 10.7)
One should perform all other <s>nyāsas</s> (placements) taught in the respective mantras,

children.text: kalpayetsvātmano dehe pīṭhaṃ dharmādibhiḥ punaḥ // Dg_10.8 = DbhP_7,40.8 //
children.translated_text: and should establish the throne in one's own body with <s>dharma</s> and the other [qualities]. (Dg 10.8)
Then, having expanded [the inner space] through <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), the wise one should meditate on the Great Goddess

children.text: hṛdambhoje mama sthāne pañcapretāsane budhaḥ // Dg_10.9 = DbhP_7,40.9 //
children.translated_text: in the lotus of the heart, in my abode, upon the seat of the five corpses (<s>pañcapretāsana</s>). (Dg 10.9)
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Sadāśiva</s>—

children.text: ete pañca mahāpretāḥ pādamūle mama sthitāḥ // Dg_10.10 = DbhP_7,40.10 //
children.translated_text: these five great corpses stand at the base of my feet. (Dg 10.10)
These are of the nature of the five elements and also of the five states;

children.text: ahaṃ tvavyaktacidrūpā tadatītāsti sarvathā // Dg_10.11 = DbhP_7,40.11 //
children.translated_text: but I, of the form of unmanifest consciousness, transcend all of these in every way. (Dg 10.11)
Therefore they have attained the state of being my seat, [as described] always in the <s>Śakti</s> <s>Tantras</s>.

children.text: dhyātvaivaṃ mānasairbhogaiḥ pūjayenmāṃ japedapi // Dg_10.12 = DbhP_7,40.12 //
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated, one should worship me with mental offerings and also perform <s>japa</s>. (Dg 10.12)
Having offered the <s>japa</s> to the glorious <s>Devī</s>, one should then establish the <s>arghya</s> (water-offering).

children.text: pātrāsādanakaṃ kṛtvā pūjādravyāṇi śodhayet // Dg_10.13 = DbhP_7,40.13 //
children.translated_text: Having arranged the vessels, one should purify the worship materials. (Dg 10.13)
The preceptor (<s>deśika</s>) [should purify] with water, with that mantra, and with the weapon-mantra;

children.text: digbandhaṃ ca purā kṛtvā gurūn natvā tataḥ param // Dg_10.14 = DbhP_7,40.14 //
children.translated_text: having first performed the binding of the directions (<s>digbandha</s>) and bowing to the <s>gurus</s>, (Dg 10.14)
and having received their permission, one should then, on the external seat,

children.text: hṛdisthāṃ bhavitāṃ mūrtiṃ mama divyāṃ manoharām // Dg_10.15 = DbhP_7,40.15 //
children.translated_text: invoke my divine, enchanting form that resides in the heart. (Dg 10.15)
One should invoke [her] onto the seat by the science of establishing the life-breath.

children.text: asanāvāhane cārghyaṃ pādyādyācamanaṃ tathā // Dg_10.16 = DbhP_7,40.16 //
children.translated_text: Seat, invocation, <s>arghya</s>, <s>pādya</s> (foot-water), and <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water), (Dg 10.16)

children.text: snānaṃ vāsodvayaṃ caiva bhūṣaṇāni ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: bathing, a pair of garments, and all ornaments,

children.text: gandhapuṣpaṃ yathāyogyaṃ dattvā devyai svabhaktitaḥ // Dg_10.17 = DbhP_7,40.17 //
children.translated_text: sandalwood paste and flowers as appropriate—one should offer these to the <s>Devī</s> with one's own devotion. (Dg 10.17)
One should properly perform the worship of the encircling deities at their places in the <s>yantra</s>.
For those unable [to worship] every day, Friday is prescribed. (Dg 10.18)
The attendant deities (<s>aṅgadevatāḥ</s>) should be contemplated as forms of the radiance of the principal <s>Devī</s>.

children.text: tatprabhāpaṭalavyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ ca vicintayet // Dg_10.19 = DbhP_7,40.19 //
children.translated_text: One should visualize the three worlds pervaded by the expanse of her radiance. (Dg 10.19)
One should worship the principal <s>Devī</s> again with repeated [offerings],

children.text: gandhādibhiḥ sugandhaistu tathā puṣpaiḥ suvāsitaiḥ // Dg_10.20 = DbhP_7,40.20 //
children.translated_text: with fragrant sandalwood and other [substances], and with sweet-smelling flowers, (Dg 10.20)
with food-offerings, libations, betel, gifts, and the like.

children.text: toṣayenmāṃ tvatkṛtena nāmnāṃ sāhasrakeṇa ca // Dg_10.21 = DbhP_7,40.21 //
children.translated_text: One should please me with the thousand names composed by you, (Dg 10.21)
with the armor [hymn], with the <s>Sūkta</s> 'I am with the <s>Rudras</s>,' O lord,
with the mantras of the <s>Devyatharvaśiras</s>, born from the <s>Hrīṃ</s>-<s>Upaniṣad</s>, (Dg 10.22)
with the great <s>vidyās</s> and great mantras—one should please me again and again.
A person with a heart melting with love should ask forgiveness of the Mother of the Universe. (Dg 10.23)
With every limb thrilling with horripilation, voice choked with tears,
with the sounds of dance, song, and the like, one should please me again and again. (Dg 10.24)
With recitations of the <s>Vedas</s> and with all the <s>Purāṇas</s>,

children.text: pratipādyā yato 'haṃ vai tasmāttaistoṣayettu mām // Dg_10.25 = DbhP_7,40.25 //
children.translated_text: since I am established through them, one should please me with those. (Dg 10.25)
One should offer me one's entire possessions, including one's own body, constantly.

children.text: nityahomaṃ tataḥ kuryādbrāhmaṇāṃśca suvāsinīḥ // Dg_10.26 = DbhP_7,40.26 //
children.translated_text: Then one should perform the daily fire-oblation, and feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and married women (<s>suvāsinīs</s>), (Dg 10.26)
young boys (<s>baṭukas</s>), the lowly, and others, regarding them as the <s>Devī</s>.

children.text: natvā punaḥ svahṛdaye vyutkrameṇa visarjayet // Dg_10.27 = DbhP_7,40.27 //
children.translated_text: Having bowed again, one should dismiss [the deity] in reverse order into one's own heart. (Dg 10.27)

children.text: sarvaṃ hṛllekhayā kuryāt pūjanaṃ mama subrata /
children.translated_text: One should perform all my worship with the <s>Hrīṃ</s>-syllable, O one of good vows.

children.text: hṛllekhā sarvamantrāṇāṃ nāyikā paramā smṛtā // Dg_10.28 = DbhP_7,40.28 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Hrīṃ</s>-syllable is held to be the supreme leader of all mantras. (Dg 10.28)
In the mirror of the <s>Hrīṃ</s>-syllable, I am always reflected.

children.text: tasmād hṛllekhayā dattaṃ sarvamantraiḥ samarpitam // Dg_10.29 = DbhP_7,40.29 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever is offered with the <s>Hrīṃ</s>-syllable is offered with all mantras. (Dg 10.29)
Having worshipped the <s>guru</s> with ornaments and the like, one should consider oneself fulfilled.

children.text: ya evaṃ pūjayeddevīṃ śrīmadbhuvanasundarīm // Dg_10.30 = DbhP_7,40.30 //
children.translated_text: One who thus worships the <s>Devī</s>, the glorious Beauty of the Universe (<s>Bhuvanasundarī</s>)— (Dg 10.30)

children.text: na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcit kadācit kvacidasti hi /
children.translated_text: for that person, nothing whatsoever is ever difficult to obtain anywhere.

children.text: dehānte tu maṇidvīpaṃ mama yātyeva sarvathā // Dg_10.31 = DbhP_7,40.31 //
children.translated_text: At the end of the body [at death], one goes to <s>Maṇidvīpa</s> (the Jewel-Island), my [abode], in all cases. (Dg 10.31)

children.text: jñeyo devīsvarūpo 'sau devā nityaṃ namanti tam /
children.translated_text: Such a person should be known as having the form of the <s>Devī</s>; the gods always bow to that one.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ rājan mahādevyāḥ prapūjanam // Dg_10.32 = DbhP_7,40.32 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, the worship of the Great Goddess has been told to you. (Dg 10.32)
Having deliberated upon all of this completely, in accordance with one's own qualification,

children.text: kuru me pūjanaṃ tena kṛtārthastvaṃ baviṣyasi // Dg_10.33 = DbhP_7,40.33 //
children.translated_text: perform my worship—thereby you will become fulfilled. (Dg 10.33)

children.text: idaṃ tu gītāśāstraṃ me nāśiṣyāya vadet kvacit /
children.translated_text: This <s>Gītā</s> scripture of mine should never be told to one who is not a disciple,

children.text: nābhaktāya pradātavyaṃ na dhūrtāya ca durhṛde // Dg_10.34 = DbhP_7,40.34 //
children.translated_text: nor should it be given to one who lacks devotion, nor to a rogue or one of wicked heart. (Dg 10.34)
Revealing this is like uncovering the Mother's breasts—

children.text: tasmādavaśyaṃ yatnena gopanīyamidaṃ sadā // Dg_10.35 = DbhP_7,40.35 //
children.translated_text: therefore it must always be carefully guarded. (Dg 10.35)

children.text: deyaṃ bhaktāya śiṣyāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya caiva hi /
children.translated_text: It may be given to a devoted disciple, to one's eldest son,

children.text: suśīlāya suveṣāya devībhaktiyutāya ca // Dg_10.36 = DbhP_7,40.36 //
children.translated_text: to one of good character, good appearance, and endowed with devotion to the <s>Devī</s>. (Dg 10.36)
If this is recited at the time of <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) in the presence of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: tṛptāstatpitaraḥ sarve prayānti paramaṃ padam // Dg_10.37 = DbhP_7,40.37 //
children.translated_text: all the ancestors, satisfied, proceed to the supreme abode. (Dg 10.37)
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Having spoken thus, that <s>Bhagavatī</s> disappeared right there.

children.text: devāśca muditāḥ sarve devīdarśanato 'bhavan // Dg_10.38 = DbhP_7,40.38 //
children.translated_text: And all the gods became delighted from the vision of the <s>Devī</s>. (Dg 10.38)

children.text: tato himālaye jajñe devī haimavatī tu sā /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Devī</s> was born on <s>Himālaya</s> as <s>Haimavatī</s>,

children.text: yā gaurīti prasiddhāsīddattā sā śaṅkarāya ca // Dg_10.39 = DbhP_7,40.39 //
children.translated_text: she who became renowned as <s>Gaurī</s> and was given to <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (Dg 10.39)
Then <s>Skanda</s> was born, and by him <s>Tāraka</s> was slain.
Previously, during the churning of the ocean, jewels appeared, O lord of men. (Dg 10.40)
There the <s>Devī</s> was praised by the gods with devotion for the sake of obtaining <s>Lakṣmī</s>;

children.text: teṣāmanugrahārthāya nirgatā tu ramā tataḥ // Dg_10.41 = DbhP_7,40.41 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of granting them grace, <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) then emerged. (Dg 10.41)
She was given by the gods to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (Viṣṇu), and through that, peace was established for him.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ rājan devīmāhātmyamuttamam // Dg_10.42 = DbhP_7,40.42 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, the supreme greatness of the <s>Devī</s> has been told to you, (Dg 10.42)
concerning the origin of <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>, which fulfills all desires.

children.text: na vācyaṃ tvetadanyasmai rahasyaṃ kathitaṃ yataḥ // Dg_10.43 = DbhP_7,40.43 //
children.translated_text: But this should not be told to another, for a secret has been spoken. (Dg 10.43)
This <s>Gītā</s>, being of a secret nature, should be carefully guarded.

children.text: sarvamuktaṃ smasena yatpṛṣṭaṃ tattvayānagha // Dg_10.44 = DbhP_7,40.44 //
children.translated_text: Everything has been told in brief—whatever was asked by you, O sinless one. (Dg 10.44)

children.text: pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ divyaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi // Dg_10.45 = DbhP_7,40.45 //
children.translated_text: It is sacred, purifying, and divine. What more do you wish to hear? (Dg 10.45)

children.text:
iti devīgītāyāṃ daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ devīgītā samāptā -
iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe saptamaskandhe devīgītāyāṃ catvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter of the <s>Devīgītā</s>. The <s>Devīgītā</s> is complete—thus the fortieth chapter of the seventh book of the glorious <s>Devī Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Devīgītā</s>.
